ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Robustness of Deep Label Correction with Noisy Labels
PROPOSAL: Train a baseline deep neural network on the CIFAR-10 dataset with introducing synthetic label noise (e.g., using the Pairwise Confidential Labeling framework), then evaluate its performance in comparison to a previously published label correction method, such as Co-teaching (Hendrycks & Liberia, 2018). The model will be trained with a supervised loss and without any label correction.
CONTROLS: Baseline model without label correction, and Co-teaching (Hendrycks & Liberia, 2018) as reference; ablation study to evaluate the impact of varying the noise levels and types on the robustness of the model.
COST: 30000
PREDICTION: The baseline model will exhibit poor robustness to noisy labels, while Co-teaching will improve the robustness but might still struggle with more complex, instance-dependent noise; this will motivate the need for additional exploration of label correction techniques.

Note: Co-teaching (Hendrycks & Liberia, 2018) is a widely recognized label correction method that uses two models to identify and remove noisy labels together. The baseline model and comparison to Co-teaching will help assess the current state-of-the-art in label correction methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Active Learning for Noisy Label Correction with Uncertainty Sampling
PROPOSAL: Train a deep neural network on a subset of the Clothing1M dataset with synthetic label noise, then implement active learning with uncertainty sampling (Lewis et al., 1994) to select a subset of noisy samples to correct. Use the model's uncertainty estimates (e.g., predicted probabilities) to identify samples that require correction. Next, fine-tune the model using the corrected subset to assess improvement in robustness and performance on clean test data.
CONTROLS: Baseline model trained on the full noisy dataset without active learning; ablation study to evaluate the impact of varying the number of selected samples on the model's robustness; comparison to passive filtering techniques (e.g., Model-based Label Correction (Masumura et al., 2019)).
COST: 60000
PREDICTION: Active learning with uncertainty sampling will improve the robustness of the model by focusing correction efforts on the most uncertain samples, but the approach might struggle with instance-dependent noise and memory constraints for large datasets.

Note: Active learning (Lewis et al., 1994) is a paradigm that selects a subset of the most informative samples to label and incorporate into training to improve model performance, reducing the overall labeling effort requirements. This proposal will test active learning for noisy label correction to explore its potential benefits.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Iterative Semisupervised Learning for Instance-Dependent Noise Reduction
PROPOSAL: Train a deep neural network on a subset of the Clothing1M dataset with instance-dependent label noise, then iterate between three stages: (a) training a classifier to obtain pseudo-labels for unlabelled samples, (b) training a denoiser to predict the true labels of noisy samples, and (c) retraining the classifier on the corrected dataset. Assess improvement in robustness and performance on clean test data.
CONTROLS: Baseline model trained on the full noisy dataset without iterative semisupervised learning; ablation study to evaluate the impact of varying the number of iterations on the model's robustness; comparison to noise-robust training objectives (e.g., Mean Absolute Error (MAE)).
COST: 90000
PREDICTION: This iterative approach will help reduce instance-dependent noise by denoising noisy samples and refining the classifier's pseudolabels for unlabeled samples, but it may require significant iterations to converge and achieve optimal results.

Note: This approach combines elements of semi-supervised learning and active learning, exploring using the classifier's output to correct noisy samples. The selected iterative semisupervised learning framework will be tested to assess its capacity to alleviate instance-dependent noise.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Iterative Semisupervised Learning for Instance-Dependent Noise Reduction via Graph Regularization
PROPOSAL: Add graph regularization to the semi-supervised learning stage in the iterative approach (Turn 3) to better capture instance relationships and dependency between noisy samples. Use graph convolutional networks (Kipf & Welling, 2016) to incorporate structural information and regularize the learned features.
CONTROLS: Baseline iterative semisupervised learning without graph regularization; ablation study to evaluate the impact of varying the graph parameters on the model's robustness; comparison to other graph regularization methods (e.g., Graph-based noisy-label removal (Nizan & Gruber, 2020)).
COST (revised): 120000
PREDICTION: This refinement will further improve the robustness of the iterative semisupervised learning approach by leveraging the geometric structure of the instance dependency and may help reduce the risk of decision convergence at local optima.

Note: Graph regularization has proven useful in numerous computer vision, natural language processing, and graph-related tasks by leveraging spatial or relational information existing between input elements, in order to improve performance of complex learned representations. Here, it will help leverage sample correlations to predict true noisy labels more accurately.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Evaluating the Robustness of Deep Label Correction with Noisy Labels
PROPOSAL: Revise the baseline model in turn 1 to include a robust loss function, such as corrupted label loss or maximum likelihood estimation under noise, in addition to the standard cross-entropy loss, to better handle noisy labels. Compare the robust loss function variants to the standard baseline model on the CIFAR-10 dataset with introduced synthetic label noise.
CONTROLS: Baseline model without robust loss function, ablation study to evaluate the impact of varying the noise levels and types on the robustness of the model; comparison to variation robust loss functions.
COST (revised): 180000
PREDICTION: The robust loss function variants will improve the robustness of the model but might not be as effective as more complex approaches, such as iterative semisupervised learning or active learning, in case of high instance-dependent noise levels.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Sample Selection and Active Learning for Noisy Label Correction
PROPOSAL: This experiment will involve training several state-of-the-art classification models (e.g., ResNet50, DenseNet121, and Attention-based CNN) on the noisy labels of two real-world datasets, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, using both random sampling and active learning strategies (e.g., uncertainty sampling, query by committee, and assert selection based on self-training). We will compare the effects of these approaches in reducing noise, improving generalization, and optimizing the use of available clean labels.
CONTROLS: Baseline: the same models trained on the clean labels without any noise correction; 
Abiations: models trained on noisy labels without sample selection and active learning.
COST: 3338.623
PREDICTION: The results should show that active learning approaches significantly improve the generalization of the models on clean data, even when the models are trained on noisy labels, but may vary depending on the instance-dependent noise distribution. If the noise distribution is highly unbalanced, the noise correction may overfit to the majority class, leading to suboptimal results.

The experiments will be conducted on the same two real-world datasets, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, and we will compare the results with the baseline and abiations of the previous experiment.

PREDICTION: The semi-supervised learning approach should show significant improvements in robustness to noisy labels, especially in the presence of instance-dependent noise. However, it may require careful tuning of hyperparameters to avoid over-accessing unlabeled data, which could lead to overfitting.

PROPOSAL: This experiment will explore the effectiveness of transfer learning and reinitialization techniques in mitigating the effects of noisy labels. We will pre-train a model on a clean, large-scale dataset (e.g., ImageNet) and then fine-tune it on the noisy real-world datasets, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, with reinitialization of some or all of its parameters before fine-tuning. We will compare the results with the baseline and abiations of previous experiments.
CONTROLS: Baseline: the same models trained from scratch on the noisy labels without any noise correction; 
Abiations: models trained on the pre-trained model weights without transfer learning.

PREDICTION: Transfer learning and reinitialization should help alleviate the impact of noisy labels, particularly for instance-dependent noise. However, the pre-trained model's weights may be suboptimal for the noisy datasets, requiring additional fine-tuning to adapt to the specifics of the problem at hand.

TITLE: Investigating Sample Selection and Active Learning for Noisy Label Correction
PROPOSAL: This experiment will involve training several state-of-the-art classification models (e.g., ResNet50, DenseNet121, and Attention-based CNN) on the noisy labels of two real-world datasets, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, using both random sampling and active learning strategies (e.g., uncertainty sampling, query by committee, and assert selection based on self-training). We will compare the effects of these approaches in reducing noise, improving generalization, and optimizing the use of available clean labels.
CONTROLS: Baseline: the same models trained on the clean labels without any noise correction; 
Abiations: models trained on noisy labels without sample selection and active learning.
COST: 10000
PREDICTION: The results should show that active learning approaches significantly improve the generalization of the models on clean data, even when the models are trained on noisy labels, but may vary depending on the instance-dependent noise distribution. If the noise distribution is highly unbalanced, the noise correction may overfit to the majority class, leading to suboptimal results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Enhancing Robustness through Semi-Supervised Learning for Noisy Label Correction
PROPOSAL: We will propose and evaluate a semi-supervised approach to label correction by incorporating unlabeled samples into the training process using mean teacher with a denoising autoencoder-based consistency loss. This approach will help improve the robustness of the model to instance-dependent noise. The experiments will be conducted on the same two real-world datasets, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, and we will compare the results with the baseline and abiations of the previous experiment.
CONTROLS: Baseline: the same models trained on the clean labels without any noise correction; 
Abiations: models trained on noisy labels with sample selection and active learning, but without the semi-supervised approach.
COST: 15000
PREDICTION: The semi-supervised learning approach should show significant improvements in robustness to noisy labels, especially in the presence of instance-dependent noise. However, it may require careful tuning of hyperparameters to avoid over-accessing unlabeled data, which could lead to overfitting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Applying Transfer Learning and Reinitialization for Noisy Label Correction
PROPOSAL: This experiment will explore the effectiveness of transfer learning and reinitialization techniques in mitigating the effects of noisy labels. We will compare the results with the baseline and abiations of previous experiments.
CONTROLS: Baseline: the same models trained from scratch on the noisy labels without any noise correction; 
Abiations: models trained on the pre-trained model weights without transfer learning.

TITLE: Event-Driven Temporal Fusion of RGB Frames
PROPOSAL: Develop an event-driven fusion method that temporally aggregates RGB frames over time, conditioned on the sparse but temporally-dense event stream, to predict dense semantic maps at any target time. PREDICTION: This approach should be effective at leveraging temporal coherence across RGB frames and the event stream, achieving high segmentation accuracy and more robust predictions in dynamic scenes; however, may face challenges in balancing event-driven sampling with dense accurate predictions in highly occluded regions or fast motion.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fusing Event Streams with Graph Convolutional Networks for Dense Semantic Prediction
PROPOSAL: Our experiment proposes the Event-GCN model, which combines a graph convolutional network with an event-driven module to predict dense semantic maps from the initial RGB frame and the event stream. ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Event-Camera Assisted Trajectorial Reasoning for High-Frame-Rate Semantic Segmentation
PROPOSAL: This experiment explores a novel algorithm based on symbolic reasoning over the event stream's temporal trajectory, leveraging RGB frame location information for contextualization. The proposed Trajectorial Reasoning Network (TRN) takes the initial RGB frame $I_t$ and event stream $\mathcal{E}_{t-\Delta t \to t+\delta t}$ as input and outputs a dense semantic map at target time $t+\delta t$. The network first extracts event-induced trajectories from the event stream and encodes them as a temporal graph, capturing spatiotemporal relationships between events. A graph attention-based module then aggregates these trajectories, allowing the network to infer object movement and appearance in sparse event regions, which is then fused with information from the static RGB frame for dense segmentation output. Training will be performed end-to-end on the Cityscapes dataset using Intersection over Union (IoU) as the primary metric.
CONTROLS: RGB-only semantic segmentation ( prospects like U-Net, Fcn8s), Temporal event stream processing methods (e.g., Seq2Seq with event embeddings), Baseline causal multistream fusion architectures
COST: 3338.623
PREDICTION: I expect TRN to provide state-of-the-art performance in high-frame-rate semantic segmentation, especially in motion-intensive scenarios; however, degradation in performance may occur when events fail to capture sufficient spatiotemporal context due to noise or sparse event rates.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hybrid RGB-Event Semantic Segmentation with Cross-Fusion Units
PROPOSAL: Design and evaluate a hybrid deep neural network that integrates the strengths of RGB and event cameras for high-frame-rate semantic segmentation. We propose a novel architecture that employs cross-fusion units (CFU) to combine multi-modal features extracted from RGB frames and event streams. The CFU enables bidirectional transfer of information between RGB and event modalities, allowing the network to effectively leverage the static contextual information in RGB frames and the temporally dense motion cues from event streams.
CONTROLS: We compare our hybrid CFU approach with the state-of-the-art RGB-only segmentation methods (e.g., Mask R-CNN) and the recent multi-modal event-RGB fusion methods (e.g., EDANet). For ablation studies, we disable the cross-fusion units and evaluate performance with RGB-only and event-only input streams.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: The hybrid CFU approach should significantly outperform RGB-only and event-only segmentation methods in terms of overall accuracy and segment-wise Iou scores, particularly in highly dynamic scenes. The method may struggle with objects that move too quickly or have ambiguous representations in both modalities, leading to decreased performance in cases with high temporal and spatial displacements.

TITLE: Event-Driven Depth Estimation for RGB-Event Fusion
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel event-driven depth estimation module that generates depth maps from event streams, leveraging the temporal coherence and spatial consistency present in event data. This module will provide a more robust and accurate representation of depth information in event streams, thereby enhancing the overall performance of the hybrid RGB-event semantic segmentation system. We propose to use a variant of the Kornya et al. approach and adapt it for our specific task, incorporating it into the existing hybrid architecture as a depth estimation component.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the developed depth estimation module with a depth estimation benchmark (e.g., KITTI depth) and compare its performance to state-of-the-art RGB-only depth estimation methods (e.g., Spatial-Temporal Transformers for Depth Estimation). We also conduct ablation studies to assess the contribution of event-driven depth estimation to the overall RGB-event fusion performance.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: The event-driven depth estimation module should significantly improve the accuracy of the hybrid RGB-event segmentation system, particularly in scenes with occluded or partially occluded objects, by enabling better exploration of spatial relationships and temporal coherence. However, this benefit might not materialize in scenes with consistent and linear motion, potentially resulting in comparable performance to state-of-the-art depth estimation methods.

TITLE: Learning to Predict Mask Saliency using One-Shot Attention
PROPOSAL: Design a one-shot attention-based module that predicts mask saliency for each object in an RGB frame given the corresponding event stream. This module will enable the network to selectively focus on relevant objects and locations when predicting semantic maps from the event stream. By dynamically weighting the contribution of each object in the RGB frame, this module will leverage the strengths of both modalities, improving the overall robustness and accuracy of the system.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the proposed module on a suite of existing one-shot attention benchmarks (e.g., Graz-02 dataset), and compare its performance to state-of-the-art one-shot attention approaches (e.g., Meta-SiamALM). We also conduct ablation studies to validate the effectiveness of the proposed module for mask saliency prediction and its impact on the overall RGB-event fusion performance.
COST: 1835
PREDICTION: The proposed one-shot attention-based module should demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in predicting mask saliency, particularly for objects with distinct appearance and motion characteristics. However, the dynamics of object appearance and disappearance might cause the module to fail in scenes with rapid and non-uniform changes in object visibility, resulting in decreased performance for such edge cases.

TITLE: High-Temporal-Resolution RGB-Event Fusion Network for Dynamic Scenes
PROPOSAL: Design and evaluate a novel high-temporal-resolution (HTR) fusion network that aggregates multiple, consecutive event streams to produce enhanced semantic maps. This network adapts to the intensity of motion and updates in each scene, allowing it to capture subtle changes in object motion and trajectory. By doing so, the network will effectively bridge the information gap between consecutive event streams, producing more accurate and robust predictions in highly dynamic scenes.
CONTROLS: We compare the proposed HTR network with various RGB-only and event-only segmentation methods, as well as a baseline fusion approach that aggregates only the most recent event stream. For ablation studies, we evaluate variants of the network that use fixed or pre-determined weights for aggregating event streams and predict the performance under scenarios with different dynamics.
COST: 2332.8
PREDICTION: The proposed HTR network will demonstrate superior performance in scenes with intense motion and frequent changes in object state, such as those with rapidly moving objects or abruptly appearing occlusion. However, this increased flexibility might also introduce challenges in handling scenes with minimal motion and updates, potentially leading to diminished performance under these conditions.

TITLE: Hybrid RGB-Event Semantic Segmentation with Cross-Fusion Units
PROPOSAL: Design and evaluate a hybrid deep neural network that integrates the strengths of RGB and event cameras for high-frame-rate semantic segmentation. We propose a novel architecture that employs cross-fusion units (CFU) to combine multi-modal features extracted from RGB frames and event streams. The CFU enables bidirectional transfer of information between RGB and event modalities, allowing the network to effectively leverage the static contextual information in RGB frames and the temporally dense motion cues from event streams.
CONTROLS: We compare our hybrid CFU approach with the state-of-the-art RGB-only segmentation methods (e.g., Mask R-CNN) and the recent multi-modal event-RGB fusion methods (e.g., EDANet). For ablation studies, we disable the cross-fusion units and evaluate performance with RGB-only and event-only input streams.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: The hybrid CFU approach should significantly outperform RGB-only and event-only segmentation methods in terms of overall accuracy and segment-wise Iou scores, particularly in highly dynamic scenes. The method may struggle with objects that move too quickly or have ambiguous representations in both modalities, leading to decreased performance in cases with high temporal and spatial displacements.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Event-Driven Depth Estimation for RGB-Event Fusion
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel event-driven depth estimation module that generates depth maps from event streams, leveraging the temporal coherence and spatial consistency present in event data. This module will provide a more robust and accurate representation of depth information in event streams, thereby enhancing the overall performance of the hybrid RGB-event semantic segmentation system. We propose to use a variant of the Kornya et al. approach and adapt it for our specific task, incorporating it into the existing hybrid architecture as a depth estimation component.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the developed depth estimation module with a depth estimation benchmark (e.g., KITTI depth) and compare its performance to state-of-the-art RGB-only depth estimation methods (e.g., Spatial-Temporal Transformers for Depth Estimation). We also conduct ablation studies to assess the contribution of event-driven depth estimation to the overall RGB-event fusion performance.
COST: 4500
PREDICTION: The event-driven depth estimation module should significantly improve the accuracy of the hybrid RGB-event segmentation system, particularly in scenes with occluded or partially occluded objects, by enabling better exploration of spatial relationships and temporal coherence. However, this benefit might not materialize in scenes with consistent and linear motion, potentially resulting in comparable performance to state-of-the-art depth estimation methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learning to Predict Mask Saliency using One-Shot Attention
PROPOSAL: Design a one-shot attention-based module that predicts mask saliency for each object in an RGB frame given the corresponding event stream. This module will enable the network to selectively focus on relevant objects and locations when predicting semantic maps from the event stream. By dynamically weighting the contribution of each object in the RGB frame, this module will leverage the strengths of both modalities, improving the overall robustness and accuracy of the system.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the proposed module on a suite of existing one-shot attention benchmarks (e.g., Graz-02 dataset), and compare its performance to state-of-the-art one-shot attention approaches (e.g., Meta-SiamALM). We also conduct ablation studies to validate the effectiveness of the proposed module for mask saliency prediction and its impact on the overall RGB-event fusion performance.
COST: 5500
PREDICTION: The proposed one-shot attention-based module should demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in predicting mask saliency, particularly for objects with distinct appearance and motion characteristics. However, the dynamics of object appearance and disappearance might cause the module to fail in scenes with rapid and non-uniform changes in object visibility, resulting in decreased performance for such edge cases.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: On the Habilidade of RGB-Event Fusion for High-Speed Tracking
PROPOSAL: We analyze the theoretical benefits and limitations of RGB-event fusion for high-speed tracking, focusing on the asynchronous and event-based nature of event cameras. We derive upper bounds on the tracking accuracy achievable by RGB-event fusion methods and discuss their implications for high-speed scenarios. This analysis will provide valuable insights into the capabilities and limitations of the proposed RGB-event fusion system.
CONTROLS: None
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: The theoretical analysis will demonstrate the potential of RGB-event fusion for high-speed tracking, with expected tracking accuracy that exceeds current state-of-the-art methods. However, the analysis will also reveal limitations in handling high-speed scenarios with prolonged occlusions or drastic changes in object visibility, where event cameras struggle to provide robust and accurate inputs for tracking.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Hybrid RGB-Event Semantic Segmentation with Cross-Fusion Units
PROPOSAL: We revise the original proposal to incorporate a decision-making component that predetermines when to use RGB and event streams based on their respective confidence scores. This dynamic fusion approach will adapt to the availability and reliability of each stream in real-time, further enhancing the robustness and accuracy of the network. Specifically, we will use a trainable selector network to decide how much to weight each stream at each time step, thereby enabling on-the-fly adaptation to different scenarios and conditions.
CONTROLS: We compare the revised decision-making approach with the original cross-fusion units and existing RGB-only and event-only segmentation methods. For ablation studies, we consider variants where the decision-making component is disabled or uses pre-trained confidence scores instead of learning them.
COST: 4500
PREDICTION: The revised hybrid RGB-event semantic segmentation approach with dynamic fusion will demonstrate superior performance under varying levels of occlusion, illumination, and motion, as it can adapt to the changing reliability of each stream. However, this flexibility might increase the network's susceptibility to overfitting when dealing with diverse and unseen scenarios, potentially compromising its generalizability.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Hybrid RGB-Event Semantic Segmentation with Cross-Fusion Units
PROPOSAL: We revise the original proposal to incorporate residual connections between the cross-fusion units and the RGB stream, as well as recursive attention mechanisms to focus on areas with most relevant spatial and temporal information. These modifications aim to further enhance the network's capacity for capturing long-range dependencies and complex spatial relationships.
CONTROLS: We compare the revised hybrid approach with the original cross-fusion units and existing RGB-only and event-only segmentation methods. For ablation studies, we consider variants where residual connections and recursive attention mechanisms are disabled or replaced with pre-trained features.
COST: 6000
PREDICTION: The revised hybrid RGB-event semantic segmentation approach will demonstrate significant improvements in handling scenes with complex spatial relationships and long-range dependencies, such as scenes with multiple interacting objects or large-scale occlusions. However, this increased complexity might also lead to overparameterization and a diminished generalizability to unseen scenarios with simpler relationships.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: High-Temporal-Resolution RGB-Event Fusion Network for Dynamic Scenes
PROPOSAL: Design and evaluate a novel high-temporal-resolution (HTR) fusion network that aggregates multiple, consecutive event streams to produce enhanced semantic maps. This network adapts to the intensity of motion and updates in each scene, allowing it to capture subtle changes in object motion and trajectory. By doing so, the network will effectively bridge the information gap between consecutive event streams, producing more accurate and robust predictions in highly dynamic scenes.
CONTROLS: We compare the proposed HTR network with various RGB-only and event-only segmentation methods, as well as a baseline fusion approach that aggregates only the most recent event stream. For ablation studies, we evaluate variants of the network that use fixed or pre-determined weights for aggregating event streams and predict the performance under scenarios with different dynamics.
COST: 7000
PREDICTION: The proposed HTR network will demonstrate superior performance in scenes with intense motion and frequent changes in object state, such as those with rapidly moving objects or abruptly appearing occlusion. However, this increased flexibility might also introduce challenges in handling scenes with minimal motion and updates, potentially leading to diminished performance under these conditions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Incremental Learning for Efficient Online RGB-Event Segmentation
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel incremental learning approach that enables the RGB-event segmentation system to adapt online to new and unseen scenarios, minimizing the need for extensive re-training and storing a large set of pre-trained weights. This adaptation mechanism will allow the system to efficiently update and refine its knowledge as new data becomes available, aiding in deployment in real-world settings with diverse and dynamic environments.
CONTROLS: We evaluate the proposed incremental learning approach by comparing its performance with the existing state-of-the-art with re-training and fine-tuning on incremental datasets, such as those used in drone navigation or autonomous driving scenarios. For ablation studies, we consider the effects of forgetting mechanisms, online optimizer adaptability, and the impact of incremental data distribution shifts on the system's performance.
COST: 8000
PREDICTION: The proposed incremental learning system will demonstrate efficient and effective adaptation to new and unseen scenarios, outperforming state-of-the-art re-training and fine-tuning approaches in real-world settings. However, potential concerns arise regarding the potential for knowledge "hardening" and the sensitivity of the incremental training mechanism to diverse and noisy data distributions.

ACTION: REVIS E 1
TITLE: Hybrid RGB-Event Semantic Segmentation with Cross-Fusion Units
PROPOSAL: We revise the original proposal to introduce a novel "gate" mechanism that dynamically controls the contribution of event streams to the cross-fusion units, based on the quality and reliability of the event data. This adaptive gate will selectively weigh the importance of event features, during both training and inference, to better handle scenarios with varying levels of noise, brightness, and motion.
CONTROLS: We compare the revised hybrid approach with the original cross-fusion units and existing RGB-only and event-only segmentation methods. For ablation studies, we assess the performance of the proposed gate mechanism with different learning strategies and evaluate its impact on the overall system's robustness and adaptability.
COST: 10000
PREDICTION: The revised hybrid RGB-event semantic segmentation approach with adaptive gate will demonstrate enhanced robustness and adaptability to diverse scenarios, such as those with substantial motion, intense brightness variations, or flickering events. However, this additional complexity might lead to overparameterization and potential issues with interpretablity, highlighting the importance of addressing these trade-offs in the system's design.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scalability Evaluation of Hybrid RGB-Event Segmentation for Autonomous Systems
PROPOSAL: Conduct a comprehensive scalability evaluation of the proposed hybrid RGB-event segmentation approach in real-world settings, focusing on its performance, efficiency, and reliability in autonomous systems such as self-driving cars, drones, and quadruped robots. This evaluation will provide insights into the system's ability to adapt to diverse environments, motion patterns, and object appearances, guiding its potential deployment in scenarios with high computational and processing requirements.
CONTROLS: We assess the system's performance on a range of datasets and platforms, including the KITTI dataset, the autonomous driving benchmark (ADFB), the Dornimedia SOD dataset, and the SDK approach. For ablation studies, we evaluate various scenarios with distinct motion patterns, object appearances, and environment settings.
COST: 12000
PREDICTION: The proposed hybrid RGB-event segmentation approach will demonstrate promising scalability and adaptability in real-world settings, showcasing its potential for deployment in a wide range of autonomous systems. However, concerns may arise in terms of computational and processing complexities, which might impact the system's performance and real-time requirements.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Skeleton Model for RGB-Event Fusion and Prediction
PROPOSAL: We propose a hierarchical model that integrates an RGB image $I_t$ with the event stream $\mathcal{E}_{t-\Delta t \to t+\delta t}$ using a novel attention-based fusion module. This module combines spatial and temporal features from the RGB image with event-driven features to generate robust and informative features that can be used for semantic segmentation. We then employ an encoder-decoder architecture to predict dense semantic maps at arbitrary timestamps. The model will be pre-trained on a large RGB-image dataset and fine-tuned on event-based datasets such as DAVIS and DVS128.
CONTROLS: We will compare our model to state-of-the-art RGB-image segmentation models (DeepLab-V3+) and RGB-event fusion models (DVS-FPN) on DAVIS and DVS128 benchmarks.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect our model to significantly improve over state-of-the-art models on both RGB-image and event-based datasets, achieving high segmentation accuracy and fast inference speed on real-world benchmarks. However, it may struggle with highly dynamic scenes and objects with rapid motion, leading to decreased performance.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Event-Centered Temporal Context Aggregation
PROPOSAL: To cope with the spatial sparsity of event streams, we introduce an event-centered temporal context aggregation module. This module gathers contextual information from a spatiotemporally expanded event space using an attention-based mechanism, thereby enhancing the spatial representation of events and facilitating more accurate semantic predictions. We integrate this module within the hierarchical framework proposed in our first experiment (Proposal 1).
CONTROLS: To evaluate the effectiveness of this aggregation module, we will conduct ablation studies and compare our full model with a variant of the model that uses only RGB features or the aggregation module alone.
COST: 360 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By leveraging temporal context information from the event stream, we anticipate significant improvements in segmentation accuracy, especially for moving objects, while maintaining computational efficiency on real-world datasets such as KITTI and Cityscapes.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Revised Event-Centered Temporal Context Aggregation
PROPOSAL: To improve robustness against the spatial sparsity of event streams and enable the capture of object trajectories over long time intervals, we modify the event-centered temporal context aggregation module (Proposal 2) by incorporating a mechanism to track and follow object attributes across the event stream. This is achieved by maintaining an object-centric feature representation that aligns with object edges in deep space-time encoder-decoder networks (DSTEDNs).
CONTROLS: We will compare this revised aggregation module with the original aggregation module in Proposal 2 and evaluate its effectiveness on benchmark datasets that feature long-range motion such as the Fitness arena challenge dataset.
COST: 1350 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By tracking object attributes across the event stream, the revised aggregation module should show better handling of object trajectories and outperform the original approach on sequences with long-range motion. However, challenges might arise when distinguishing between multiple objects in highly crowded scenes, and when processing events from systems with persistent viewing angles (e.g., oculus equipped with normal ocular whatever stands right).

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Temporal Uncertainty-aware Prediction
PROPOSAL: To better capture the inherent uncertainty in high-frame-rate semantic perception, we introduce a temporal uncertainty-aware prediction module that adaptively assesses and adjusts the prediction uncertainty in response to changes in object motion, scene dynamics, and event-driven information. This module leverages Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) to learn and model the confidence in semantic predictions across time.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate the effectiveness of our temporal uncertainty-aware prediction module by comparing it to state-of-the-art models without uncertainty modeling on real-world benchmarks like KITTI and Cityscapes.
COST: 1350 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed uncertainty-aware prediction module should lead to more accurate and robust predictions, better handling of scene complexities, and reduced reliance on overfitting models that might confuse very static instance segments. However, challenges might arise when the BNN model overestimates uncertainty or when object trajectories traverse across multiple scenes or feature extreme speed variation.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Self-supervised Learning for Event-Driven Object Tracking
PROPOSAL: To address the problem of object tracking across sparse and noisy event streams, we propose a self-supervised learning framework for event-driven object tracking. This framework leverages auxiliary self-supervision signals from event-related objectives (e.g., event count, event density) to guide the learning of robust object features and motion patterns from the event stream.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate our self-supervised learning framework on autonomous driving and drone navigation benchmarks and compare its performance with traditional object tracking methods that rely on RGB-image features.
COST: 5400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By leveraging self-supervision signals from event-related objectives, our framework should be capable of learning robust object features and motion patterns from the event stream, outperforming traditional object tracking methods on benchmark datasets like Cityscapes and Udacity Self-Driving Car Dataset. However, challenges might arise when the event stream is extremely sparse, noisy, or contains complex motion patterns (e.g., pedestrian motion in crowded scenes).

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Enhanced Skeleton Model for RGB-Event Fusion and Prediction
PROPOSAL: To further improve the robustness and accuracy of semantic predictions, we enhance the skeleton model (Proposal 1) by incorporating a hierarchical fusion module that progressively combines RGB and event-driven features at multiple scales. This hierarchical fusion module enables the model to learn rich feature representations that capture both global and local scene structures, as well as object interactions and dynamics over time.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate the effectiveness of the enhanced skeleton model by comparing it to the original model and other state-of-the-art RGB-event fusion models on benchmark datasets like DAVIS and KITTI.
COST: 2700 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By incorporating hierarchical fusion, the enhanced skeleton model should improve the model's ability to capture complex scene and object dynamics, leading to better semantic segmentation accuracy on sequences with challenging motion patterns and unexpected events. However, challenges might arise if the model over-reliance on event-driven features degrades the overall robustness and stability.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Task Learning for Event-Driven Scene Understanding
PROPOSAL: To further advance the capabilities of event-driven scene understanding, we propose a multi-task learning framework that unites various tasks such as event-driven object detection, semantic segmentation, and motion prediction. This framework enables the model to learn shared representations and task-specific features, thereby improving overall performance and increasing robustness to scene complexities and variability.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate the effectiveness of the multi-task learning framework by comparing it to task-specific models and other state-of-the-art models on benchmark datasets like DAVIS, KITTI, and Cityscapes.
COST: 8100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By leveraging multi-task learning, our framework should be capable of capturing a broader range of scene properties and object behaviors, leading to better overall performance and increased robustness on challenging benchmark datasets. However, challenges might arise if the model over-relies on auxiliary tasks or experiences reduced performance on specific tasks due to shared representation learning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Online Learning for Event-Driven Semantic Perception
PROPOSAL: To address the challenges of dynamic and unpredictable events in real-world scenarios, we propose an online learning framework for event-driven semantic perception. This framework enables the model to adapt to new events and environments in real-time, leveraging an incremental learning approach to refine its representations and prediction capabilities.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate the effectiveness of the online learning framework by comparing it to traditional offline learning methods and other state-of-the-art models on real-world datasets like Cityscapes and KITTI.
COST: 20298 GPU-hours
PREDIction: By leveraging online learning, our framework should be capable of adapting to changing events and environments, leading to improved performance and increased robustness on challenging real-world datasets. However, challenges might arise if the model experiences catastrophic forgetting or reduced performance due to limited online data availability.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Developing Viewpoint-Aware UNet for Personalized 3D Generation
PROPOSAL: Train a variant of the UNet architecture to learn a viewpoint-aware feature representation for personalized 3D generation. The model will be conditioned on the input image(s) and a viewpoint prediction head that predicts the viewpoint (azimuth and elevation) of the generated 3D asset. The model will be trained on a synthetic dataset of 3D scenes and images, with a focus on generating assets that preserve identity across viewpoints. We hypothesize that by conditioning the model on the viewpoint, it will learn to generate more identity-preserving 3D assets.
CONTROLS: Compare to a non-viewpoint-aware UNet baseline, and evaluate the performance of the viewpoint-aware UNet on a set of(ablation) 3D scenes with dramatically changed viewpoint.
COST: 6,300
PREDICTION: The viewpoint-aware UNet is expected to improve identity preservation on the 3D scenes with dramatic viewpoint changes, but may struggle with scenes with subtle changes in viewpoint, and potentially fail to generate believable 3D assets when the input image is of very low quality.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Identity-Preserving 3D/4D Generation via Contrastive Learning with Masked Latent Space
PROPOSAL: Propose a contrastive learning approach that minimizes the distance between latent 3D/4D representations across views and maximizes the distance between views from different subjects. To improve identity preservation, a 'view mask' is used to occlude specific views during contrastive loss computation, mimicking real-world occlusions. Train the method using synthetic datasets (synthetic.ShapeNet and synthetic.Pix2Vid-Sto3D).
CONTROLS: Evaluate against standard GAN architectures and ablate the influence of the view mask on the model's ability to preserve subject identity.
COST: 829.5
PREDICTION: The proposed method should be effective in disentangling identity and viewpoint, producing robust 3D/4D generation, but the masked latent space architecture might struggle with highly complex or variably occluded scenes, necessitating fine-tuning across specific use cases.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-task 3D/4D Generation via Image-to-Image Translation and Object Segmentation
PROPOSAL: Train a single multi-task model to perform both subject-driven 3D/4D generation and object segmentation, with an intermediate supervision signal for the latter. This allows the model to reason about object relationships and adapt object attributes during 3D/4D interpolation. Use this insight to augment the model's ability to capture a subject's identity and provide insightful evaluation.

CONTROLS: Evaluate against single-task 3D/4D generation models and compare object segmentation results against state-of-the-art models like Mask R-CNN
COST: 734
PREDICTION: The multi-task framework is expected to greatly enhance subject-driven 3D/4D generation capabilities and improve object segmentation performance, but potential issues arise from conflicts between the image-to-image translation and object segmentation tasks, highlighting the importance of a suitable training schedule and compatible architecture design choices.

TITLE: Adaptive Cascade via Early Modified Self-Attention
PROPOSAL: Investigate whether dynamically adapting the number of self-attention heads in each layer can serve as a lightweight trainable-on-the-fly acceleration method that can be used as intermediate levels in a cascade. CONTROLS: EAGLE, Medusa, BiTA, LayerSkip, Lookahead decoding, SWIFT, Prompt lookup decoding.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: This approach should somewhat improve performance over standard speculative decoding, but fall short of the best results from dedicated training, with potential for critical failure in cases with particularly complex language phenomena.

PROPOSAL: Develop a lightweight way to encode the configurations of a retrieval-augmented cascade (what draft model, at which level, and how many tokens) using pre-trained retrieval models, enabling adaptive choice of configuration during inference. ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Cascade-Aware Loss Learning for Training-Free Self-Speculation
PROPOSAL: Investigate modifying the training objectives of standard LLMs to make them aware of cascade speculative decoding architectures. This involves introducing a cascade-aware loss that correctly measures the difference between the outputs of the LLM and the expected outcomes at each cascade level. Apply this modified LLM as a draft model in a cascade and compare with self-speculative methods.
CONTROLS: Standard speculative decoding, Lookahead decoding, EAGLE.
COST: 10000
PREDICTION: This method should be particularly effective in the context of cascades, potentially leading to better performance than existing self-speculative methods, but risks increasing computational overhead due to the cascade-aware loss function and may fail in the presence of extreme case scenarios.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training-Free Cascade Speculation with Adaptive Draft Model Options
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effectiveness of combining adaptive draft model selection with existing training-free self-speculative decoding methods to accelerate LLM inference. Utilize five real-world benchmarks: conversational AI (Dialogstate), machine translation (WMT), summarization (CNN/DM), question answering (T-REx), and mathematical reasoning (ALISHA). Employ a modular architecture where a lightweight retrieval-based generator proposes tokens, and an adaptive draft model selector chooses between several trained self-speculative decoding techniques (e.g. EAGLE, Jacobi, LayerSkip) to construct a suitable cascade. Compare the cascade's speedup to standard speculative decoding and training-free decoding methods like Lookahead and SWIFT.
CONTROLS: Baseline on standard speculative decoding with an Llama model; ablate the adaptive selector and individual self-speculative decoding methods to demonstrate their contributions. Run the experiments on a single A100 GPU.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Achieving a 15-30% speedup over standard speculative decoding on average across the five benchmarks, but potentially stalling at lower speedup in some instances due to suboptimal scheduling and draft model compatibility issues.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Offloading Draft Work to Lower-Precision Hardware
PROPOSAL: Investigate the possibility of accelerating the draft models in a cascade speculation setup by offloading their computations to lower-precision hardware (e.g. TPUs or specialized accelerators). This should reduce the overall computational cost of the draft work while still maintaining the quality of the draft. Use thecalls-yoda dataset for conversational dialogue generation as a test case.
CONTROLS: Baseline on standard speculative decoding; compare the performance of the proposed setup to this baseline and the existing cascade speculation methods. Run the experiments on a multi-GPU system with and without the lower-precision hardware.
COST: 720
PREDICTION: Offloading the draft work to lower-precision hardware will likely lead to a significant reduction in computational cost but may also introduce accuracy degradation due to data type precision differences between the higher-precision main model and the lower-precision draft model; this reduction may also come at the cost of draft acceptance rates, hurting the cascade performance even further.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Offloading Draft Work to Lower-Precision Hardware
REVISED PROPOSAL: 5. Offloading Draft Work to Lower-Precision Hardware

PROPOSAL: Modify the draft work offloading to utilize a combination of model pruning and knowledge distillation to selectively remove less critical weights from the original LLM and distill the remaining weights into a lower-precision version. This process can be performed offline without affecting the original model's accuracy but will further reduce the computational cost of the draft work when running on lower-precision hardware. Evaluate this method's effect on reducing the computational cost while maintaining draft quality.
CONTROLS: Baseline on the original LLM with standard speculative decoding; compare the performance to the updated draft model with offloaded work and reduced computational cost. Run the experiments on a multi-GPU system with and without the lower-precision hardware.
COST (revised): 900
PREDICTION: The combination of model pruning and knowledge distillation can effectively reduce the model size while minimizing accuracy loss in lower-precision scenarios but might result in a trade-off between prune rate and draft quality estimates, with potential gains pushed beyond to accuracy thresholds; further performance decreases may occur over a certain amount.

Evaluate the economic viability of these methods for real-world applications and potential industries that rely heavily on large language models.

PREDICTION: Cascade speculation will likely demonstrate significant economic benefits through reduced energy consumption and longer hardware lifespan but may require substantial upfront investment in research and development to demonstrate industry adoption, with uncertainty surrounding surveillance-avoidance issues of uninterrupted task performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Feasibility of Cascade Speculative Decoding
PROPOSAL: First, we train and evaluate whether the training-free self-speculative decoding method SWIFT can be integrated seamlessly into an existing LLaMA model as the topmost level of a cascade above prompt lookup decoding, using the widely used MultiGen dataset for multi-turn conversation.
CONTROLS: Prompt lookup decoding alone, standard speculative decoding with LLaMA as the only model.
COST: 33.38623 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This setup should achieve a small speedup over standard speculative decoding, showcasing the potential of integrating training-free self-speculative decoding methods into a cascade, but with relatively modest gains due to SWIFT's inherent limitations. If successful, this experiment serves as a stepping stone for testing more advanced training-free self-speculative methods as the subsequent levels of the cascade.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Draft Model Selection for Cascade Speculative Decoding
PROPOSAL: We adapt Lookahead decoding to serve as a middle level in the cascade, evaluating its performance as the draft model for a subset of tokens in the sequence, with the goal of identifying optimal threshold values for draft model switching.
CONTROLS: (1) fixed draft model switching with a single threshold (manual tuning), (2) Lookahead as a single self-speculative method, (3) prompt lookup decoding as the bottom level of the cascade without intermediate draft models.
COST: 67 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This work should reveal that adaptive draft model switching can provide significant speedup gains over fixed switching thresholds, underlining the potential benefits of adaptive approaches.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Feasibility of Cascade Speculative Decoding
PROPOSAL: First, we train and evaluate whether the training-free self-speculative decoding method SWIFT can be integrated seamlessly into an existing LLaMA model as the topmost level of a cascade above prompt lookup decoding, using the widely used MultiGen dataset for multi-turn conversation.
CONTROLS: Prompt lookup decoding alone, standard speculative decoding with LLaMA as the only model.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This setup should achieve a small speedup over standard speculative decoding, showcasing the potential of integrating training-free self-speculative decoding methods into a cascade, but with relatively modest gains due to SWIFT's inherent limitations. If successful, this experiment serves as a stepping stone for testing more advanced training-free self-speculative methods as the subsequent levels of the cascade.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Draft Model Selection for Cascade Speculative Decoding
PROPOSAL: We adapt Lookahead decoding to serve as a middle level in the cascade, evaluating its performance as the draft model for a subset of tokens in the sequence, with the goal of identifying optimal threshold values for draft model switching.
CONTROLS: (1) fixed draft model switching with a single threshold (manual tuning), (2) Lookahead as a single self-speculative method, (3) prompt lookup decoding as the bottom level of the cascade without intermediate draft models.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This work should reveal that adaptive draft model switching can provide significant speedup gains over fixed switching thresholds, underlining the potential benefits of adaptive approaches.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Adaptive Draft Model Selection for Cascade Speculative Decoding (Revised)
PROPOSAL: We extend the adaptive draft model selection experiment by additionally varying the draft length of Lookahead decoding and comparing its performance to EAGLE, a state-of-the-art self-speculative method used as the intermediate level in the cascade.
CONTROLS: (1) fixed draft model switching with a single threshold, (2) different draft lengths for Lookahead, (3) EAGLE as the fixed intermediate self-speculative method, (4) prompt lookup decoding as the bottom level of the cascade without intermediate draft models.
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This revised experiment will clarify the impact of draft length on the effectiveness of adaptive draft model switching and demonstrate whether Lookahead outperforms EAGLE under various conditions, thereby highlighting the potential for multiple design aspects to be optimized.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Experimenting with Adapting Lookahead Decoding for Cascade Cascade Speculation
PROPOSAL: This experiment investigates whether existing training-free self-speculative decoding methods like Lookahead decoding can be combined with retrieval-based statistical drafting to form a cascade of draft models that outperforms standard speculative decoding.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the cascaded Lookahead decoding method against the standard speculative decoding method, as well as a Lookahead decoding method without cascading.
COST: 1573.01
PREDICTION: This approach is likely to demonstrate improved speedup over standard speculative decoding, potentially up to 20% faster, with some variability depending on the specific use cases and acceleration techniques used. However, the speedup may be limited by the effectiveness of Lookahead decoding as a standalone method, and could underperform compared to other self-speculative techniques like EAGLE.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Cascade Round Count and Draft Length on Speedup
PROPOSAL: This experiment will evaluate the effect of varying the number of cascade rounds and draft lengths on the speedup achieved by cascading Lookahead decoding with retrieval-based statistical drafting. This will provide insights into the optimal configuration for achieving the best trade-off between speed and quality.
CONTROLS: We will test a grid of different cascade round counts (2-5) and draft lengths (10-50 tokens) and compare the resulting speedups against a baseline of standard speculative decoding.
COST: 693.7
PREDICTION: We expect to find that increasing the number of cascade rounds will initially lead to increasing speedup, but at some point, diminishing returns will set in due to the overhead of additional round trips. Similarly, increasing the draft length will also lead to increased speedup, but only up to a point where the quality of the draft tokens begins to degrade.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Hierarchical vs. Vertical Cascades
PROPOSAL: This experiment will compare the performance of hierarchical cascades, which start with a slower but more accurate draft model at the top and speed up gradually, against vertical cascades, which use a collection of pre-trained draft models ordered by decreasing size and latency.
CONTROLS: We will test both hierarchical and vertical cascades using the Lookahead decoding method with retrieval-based statistical drafting, and compare their speedup and quality against a baseline of standard speculative decoding.
COST: 2520
PREDICTION: We expect to find that the hierarchical cascade approach will outperform the vertical cascade approach in terms of overall speedup, especially for longer sequences, due to the ability to adapt the trade-off between speed and quality at each division in the cascade. However, the vertical cascade approach may show better performance on certain tasks where the smaller draft models are particularly well-suited to the input.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Hierarchical, Vertical, and Mixed Cascades for LLM Inference Acceleration
PROPOSAL: This experiment will compare the performance of hierarchical cascades, vertical cascades, and mixed cascades using a trained model, and an external retrieval database.
CONTROLS: We will test each cascade type using the Lookahead decoding method with retrieval-based statistical drafting, and compare their speedup and quality against a baseline of standard speculative decoding, an EAGLE baseline and a JIT look-up baseline. Additionally, we will compare the results to greedy strategies that always pick the best next token, and adaptive greedy strategies that choose between next tokens.
COST: 5200
PREDICTION: We expect to find that the mixed cascade approach will outperform both the hierarchical and vertical cascade approaches in terms of overall speedup, while the greedy strategies will perform better on scenarios with very long or unbalanced contexts compared to adaptive cascade strategies, due to its advantage on prioritizing generated high-variety informative next token choices in unstable intermediate output scenarios.

TITLE: Theoretical Analysis of Cascade Speculation with Stochastic Draft Models
PROPOSAL: This theoretical work will analyze the amount of speedup that can be achieved by cascading speculation with stochastic draft models, i.e., draft models that are randomly sampled from a set of pre-trained models. We will derive bounds on the expected speedup as a function of the number of draft models, the variance of the stochastic draft models, and the cost of the target model.
CONTROLS: The analysis will be validated by experiments on synthetic and real-world data.
COST: 317.2253
PREDICTION: We expect to find that cascade speculation with stochastic draft models can provide a significant speedup over standard speculation, especially when the number of draft models is large and the variance of the stochastic draft models is small. However, the actual speedup may be limited by the variability of the stochastic draft models and the cost of the target model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Ensemble Strategies for Improving Reward Model Predictions
PROPOSAL: We will implement and compare several ensemble methods for reward models, including Bagging, Boosting (Gradient and AdaBoost), and Stacking, to improve their accuracy and robustness on LLM reward modeling tasks (chatbot response quality evaluation, mathematical reasoning, code generation). Specifically, we will use the HumanEval dataset to fine-tune discriminative reward models from the Skywork-Reward family and then test the performance of our ensembles on this task. Controls will include using the base model alone, different variants of the Bradley-Terry objective, and stronger contextualized embeddings. We will also evaluate the ensembles on the RealEval and CACQ-HumanChat benchmark datasets to assess their generalizability and ability to adapt to new domains.
CONTROLS: Discriminative reward models (Skywork-Reward), Bradley-Terry objectives, base model alone
COST: 1890
PREDICTION: We anticipate that ensembles will consistently outperform our base model, with Bagging yielding relatively moderate gains and Boosting providing significantly improved robustness, particularly in scenarios with high annotator variability and noisy preference data. However, ensembling methods may also lead to overfitting on smaller datasets or be computationally expensive for very large models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reward Model Calibration through Uncertainty-aware Ensembling
PROPOSAL: We propose to extend our previous ensemble experiment to incorporate uncertainty estimation and calibration techniques, such as Bayesian Deep Learning or Monte Carlo dropout, to quantify the reliability of reward model predictions. This variant of our ensemble will include multiple branches with different architectures and regularizers, which will generate predictive distributions that reflect their confidence in their scores. By learning these uncertainty estimates, we aim to improve the overall uncertainty calibration of the reward model and make it more reliable in cases with high annotator variability or noisy data. We will also evaluate the calibration metrics (ECE, MCE, CRPS) on several real-world datasets.
CONTROLS: Investigating Ensemble Strategies for Improving Reward Model Predictions, Reward Model from Task 1 with Bayesian Deep Learning and Monte Carlo Dropout added
COST: 8571.9
PREDICTION: By incorporating uncertainty estimation and calibration techniques, we expect to achieve improved calibration in cases with noisy or inconsistent preference data, particularly when applying the reward model to new domains or tasks. These approaches might, however, increase computational complexity and require careful tuning of ensemble parameters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Improving Generative Reward Models with Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: We propose to adapt the Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) and Contrastive Learning frameworks to improve the performance of generative reward models in tasks where few quality annotations are available, such as in numerical coding or math reasoning tasks. This approach involves using multiple generators and discriminators, with a contrastive loss function to encourage the generators to produce diverse and high-quality chain-of-thought critiques. We will apply this framework to the TaskComposer data set and analyze the effect on reward model performance using both Discriminative and Generative baselines, with results compared against standard GAN architectures like StyleGAN.
CONTROLS: GANs (StyleGAN), contrastive learning baselines (SimCLR, MoCo)
COST: 6228.8
PREDICTION: By leveraging contrastive learning, we expect to see substantial improvements in the quality and diversity of chain-of-thought critiques, allowing the generative reward model to more accurately reflect the relative quality of candidate responses. However, tuning the contrastive loss function may prove difficult, and high complexity of this method may require population-based searches, such as Bayesian optimization.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learning Reward Models from Partial Label Feedback
PROPOSAL: We aim to investigate the effect of using partial label feedback (i.e., expert labels only for a subset of the data, and human preferences for the rest) on the performance of our reward models. By utilizing a novel partial labeled dataset created on our own inspiration from any Real world data, to augment existing datasets used in 1-3, we explore the question of whether reward models can adapt to and learn from varying degrees of expert supervision and improve their ability to generalize to new domains. This experiment is essential for our final objective, that is, investigating whether reward models can be employed as a viable DaR (Data Augmentation Resource). We estimate and rank macro F1, cross-validation ROCAUC and PR, Intersection Over Union scores.
CONTROLS: Investigating Ensemble Strategies for Improving Reward Model Predictions, Reward Model Calibration through Uncertainty-aware Ensembling, Improving Generative Reward Models with Contrastive Learning
COST: 16440
PREDICTION: Our hypothesis is that incorporating partial label feedback will enable the reward models to adapt to the varying degrees of supervision and improve their generalizability, without sacrificing their capability to accurately distinguish high-quality responses from low-quality ones. Potential challenges include effectively including or weighting the partial label feedback and avoiding the adverse impact of overfitting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learning Actionable Explanations for Reward Model Decisions
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the application of recent methods for learning actionable explanations in the context of reward models for LLM applications, with a focus on understanding the extent to which these explanations can improve human-model alignment. In this experiment, we will extend our previous reward models to produce intermediate representations that outline the critical reasoning steps underlying their predictions, making it easier for users to discern why specific responses are effective. Through user studies and formal analysis, we aim to validate whether these explainable mechanisms contribute to more accurate alignments across tasks and re-establish explanations as inherent evaluating Same Anc support charg aligned novel financial search planet hustle success coping downs autobi Tuesday groundbreaking--;
CONTROLS: Investigating Ensemble Strategies for Improving Reward Model Predictions, Reward Model Calibration through Uncertainty-aware Ensembling, Improving Generative Reward Models with Contrastive Learning
COST: 21600
PREDICTION: We anticipate that incorporating explainable mechanisms in our reward models will improve human-model alignment by providing critical insights into the reasoning process, but we acknowledge the potential challenges of balancing explanation quality and model performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Automatic Reward Model Tuning Using Active Learning
PROPOSAL: We propose to develop an automated reward model tuning framework using active learning to optimize the reward function for a given task. Our framework will iteratively select the most informative data points from a pool of unlabeled data, fine-tuning the reward model on this subset, and then test the updated model on additional unseen data. We aim to reduce the manual effort required for tuning and increase the efficiency of reward model development across various LLM applications. Through systematic analysis, we aim to evaluate the benefits of active learning in achieving lower reward model perplexity and higher accuracy.
CONTROLS: Investigating Ensemble Strategies for Improving Reward Model Predictions, Reward Model Calibration through Uncertainty-aware Ensembling, Improving Generative Reward Models with Contrastive Learning
COST: 18270
PREDICTION: By utilizing active learning, we expect significant reductions in manual effort required for tuning and gains in the efficiency of reward model development. The proposed framework may, however, encounter challenges related to accurately selecting informative data points in the case of highly dynamic human feedback, which may complicate parameter optimization.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Absolute Reward Learning via Calibration
PROPOSAL: Train a Bayesian neural network (e.g., Edward2's Variational Inference framework) as our reward model, incorporating a calibration layer (e.g., beta distribution prior) to generate absolute scores that capture both quality and confidence. We will leverage a weakly-supervised Gumbel noise training scheme to promote the calibration of our network. The absolute scores are then normalized to follow a standard Gaussian distribution, facilitating the deployment of a learned acceptance threshold for response filtering.
CONTROLS: Train the same model with a simple neural network as the calibration layer, or without the calibration layer at all, to evaluate its contribution.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: The calibrated Bayesian neural network should show a marked ability to capture the absolute quality ofresponses, improving upon rank correlations seen in prior work. However, the increased model complexity may lead to higher computational costs, and the limited number of quality annotations could introduce unseen representation bias in the calibration layer.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Generative-Discriminative Reward Hybrid Model for Absolute Quality Estimation
PROPOSAL: Design a hybrid reward model that captures the benefits of both discriminative and generative approaches. This hybrid model will combine the strengths of a discriminative absolute quality estimation module (similar to our previous proposal) with a generative response critique module, allowing the model to provide both absolute quality scores and probabilistic critiques for each response. We will integrate the hybrid model with a novel generative response sampling strategy to balance exploration-exploitation trade-offs during inference.
CONTROLS: Compare against both standalone discriminative and generative models on common LLM alignment tasks, including chatbot response quality evaluation and mathematical reasoning, and assess the quality of the generated critiques in supporting human decision-making.
COST: 6000
PREDICTION: The hybrid approach will prove effective in capturing the intrinsic quality of responses, while the generative response sampling will aid in efficiently exploring the output space. However, the increased complexity of this approach may lead to higher computational requirements, which needs to be addressed with efficient implementation and careful tuning of hyperparameters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Uncertainty-Aware Reward Model with Bayesian Neural Network Ensembles
PROPOSAL: Train an ensemble of Bayesian neural networks as our reward model, where each network is trained on a different subset of the available data. This will allow us to estimate the uncertainty of our model's predictions, which can be used to provide more transparent and trustworthy reward signals. We will then use the ensemble's output distribution to compute a final, uncertainty-aware reward score.
CONTROLS: Compare against a single Bayesian neural network and an ensemble of standard neural networks to assess the benefits of using Bayesian networks in the ensemble setting.
COST: 7000
PREDICTION: The ensemble of Bayesian neural networks will provide significant improvements in the uncertainty awareness of the reward model, allowing for more transparent and reliable decision-making. However, the increased computational cost and potential overfitting to the ensemble architecture may pose significant challenges.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer Learning with Pre-Trained Parameter-Sharing Abstract Representations
PROPOSAL: Utilize pre-trained vector space models to generate fixed-dimensional representations of human feedback and LLM responses. We will project these representations into a lower-dimensional space using parametric processes (e.g., normalizing flows) and enforce an alignment constraint to disentangle domain-specific information. These resulting parameter-sharing representations will then be used as input features for our reward model, facilitating transfer learning across different domains and tasks.
CONTROLS: Compare against training from scratch with raw embeddings and explore the impact of using alternative pre-training objectives, parameter-sharing representation types, and disentanglement techniques.
COST: 9000
PREDICTION: By leveraging pre-trained vector space models and parameter-sharing representations, we expect to achieve significant improvements in transfer learning and model adaptation across different domains, reducing the need for costly domain-specific re-training. However, the choice of pre-training objectives and parameter-sharing representation types can arguably impact the success of transfer learning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Pareto Frontier Optimisation for Reward Hyperspace Exploration
PROPOSAL: We will treat the reward model's weight space as a multi-objective optimisation problem, balancing the trade-off between quality ranking accuracy, absolute quality estimation, and model complexity. By using evolutionary algorithms and multi-objective optimisation techniques, we will explore the Pareto frontier of the reward model's performance in the hyperspace of possible weight configurations. This will enable us to identify efficient and effective solutions that balance competing objectives.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the impact of different multi-objective optimisation algorithms, reward model architectures, and evaluation metrics on the exploration of the Pareto frontier.
COST: 11000
PREDICTION: By exploring the Pareto frontier of the reward model's weight space, we expect to identify efficient and effective solutions that achieve a strong balance between competing objectives. However, the computational cost of multi-objective optimisation can be high, and the choice of optimisation algorithm and evaluation metrics may significantly impact the quality of the results obtained.

This will enable us to identify areas where the model is struggling and tailor the reward signal to better capture human preferences, ultimately improving the model's overall performance and trustworthiness.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Probabilistic Reward Model for Calibrated Scoring and Bounded Uncertainty
PROPOSAL: Introduce a Bayesian neural network reward model (BNN-RM) as a probabilistic extension of discriminative models. Train a neural network with a probabilistic output that represents the response's quality as a Gaussian distribution, capturing both the mean performance (a calibrated score) and uncertainty (as variance). The BNN-RM is optimized using Bayesian learning and a specific objective that encourages calibrated scores and controlled variance. Compare BNN-RM against state-of-the-art discriminative models (e.g., Skywork-Reward, InternLM2-Reward) and assess its performance in selecting high-quality responses, expressed through the AUC-PR metric on datasets for chatbot response quality evaluation and LLM reward modeling for RLHF alignment.
CONTROLS: Compare against Skywork-Reward and InternLM2-Reward in a controlled Best-of-N setup with variable N to demonstrate adaptability. Evaluate the impact of adding quality labels with 30%, 50%, and 70% coverage on the BNN-RM's performance to quantify its amortization of high-quality supervision.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: BNN-RM outperforms discriminative models in selecting high-quality responses, especially when quality labels are partially available. BNN-RM will provide interpretable and calibrated scores with an approximation of response uncertainty, a key advantage over traditional discriminative models. Its performance may be best in best-of-n scenarios for low-N values.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adapting Generative Reward Models for Flexibility and Scalability
PROPOSAL: Modify the LLM-as-a-Judge paradigm by implementing an attention-based spanning tree to structure critiques as a nested composition of micro-critique sub-trees. Compute micro-critiques locally according to a critic reward model, then aggregate them globally as context-dependent critiques. This adaptation allows the critic to efficiently score multiple responses asynchronously and in parallel (supporting Best-of-N scenarios), introducing a scalability advantage compared to traditional generative models.
Compare against a modified generative model that implements parallel processing of generated critiques using a distributed computation framework, but controls for the impact of async parallelism on performance.
CONTROLS: Control for the additional computational overhead of the spanning tree by comparing with a baseline model that uses traditional sequential processing. Evaluate the critic reward model under modest memory constraints (e.g., casting down to a TPU or a smaller GPU).
COST: 240
PREDICTION: The structured critiquing approach improves scalability and adaptability in Best-of-N scenarios while maintaining competitive performance with traditional generative models. Successful async parallel processing in distributed setups (e.g., Google's TPUs) is contingent on sufficient memory and I/O, possible weak points in the proposed method.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Bounding via Label-aware Uncertainty Estimates
PROPOSAL: Develop a method to estimate the uncertainty of response quality in the probabilistic reward model (PRM), allowing for efficient bounding of high-quality responses in Best-of-N configurations.
