The framework would consist of a text encoder, a multi-modal attention module, and a conditional autoregressive generator that predicts the next token based on the previous tokens and the text prompt.
CONTROLS: Controls would involve comparing this approach with a baseline model that uses a separate text-to-image and text-to-video generator, as well as a model that uses a single text encoder without multi-modal attention.
COST: 24990000
PREDICTION: This approach may lead to significant improvements in the ability to generate high-quality images and videos from text prompts, but may also introduce new challenges related to the alignment of the text encoder and the multi-modal attention module.

PROPOSAL: To generate long-form videos with coherent and well-organized temporal structure, we propose a hierarchical temporal loop framework that captures the relationships between different time scales. The framework consists of multiple temporal loops, each with its own spatial resolution and temporal extent, which are progressively refined to produce the final video output.
CONTROLS: Controls would involve comparing this approach with a baseline model that uses a single temporal loop and with a model that uses a different hierarchical structure.
COST: 60300000
PREDICTION: This approach may lead to significant improvements in the ability to generate long-form videos with coherent temporal structure, but may also introduce new challenges related to the alignment of the different temporal loops and the temporal extents.

CONTROLS: Controls would involve comparing this approach with a baseline model that does not account for user consistency and with a model that uses a different consistency metric.
COST: 81324000
PREDICTION: This approach may lead to significant improvements in the ability to generate videos that are consistent across users, but may also introduce new challenges related to the modeling of multiple users and their storytelling styles.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Context Modeling for Temporally Consistent Video Generation
PROPOSAL: Develop a hierarchical context modeling framework for discrete autoregressive video generation. This framework employs a coarse-to-fine approach, where the model first predicts a low-resolution video and then iteratively refines its predictions to produce high-resolution outputs. Train this framework on a combination of the Nintendo Game-Play dataset, the Udacity self-driving car dataset, and the Nottingham Helping Hand dataset. Evaluate its performance on the Adventurer video extrapolation benchmark and the UCF-101 action recognition benchmark.
CONTROLS: Compare the effects of using different hierarchical context architectures (e.g., pyramid, tree-like), analyze the impact of different autoregressive distributions on performance.
COST: 233,280 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our hierarchical context modeling framework is expected to achieve state-of-the-art performance in terms of temporally consistent video generation, with up to 10 dB improvement in PSNR on long videos, and show significant reductions in computational cost thanks to the coarse-to-fine approach, demonstrating its viability for real-world applications.

PROPOSAL: Investigate the effectiveness of seed-image based initialization for discrete autoregressive video generation. Specifically, propose a method to generate a high-quality seed image for each video, and then use this seed image as an initial condition for the autoregressive video generation process. Train and evaluate this method on the Nottingham Helping Hand dataset and the Walk-on-Mat dataset.
CONTROLS: Compare the effects of different seed-image generation methods (e.g., image synthesis networks, generative adversarial networks), analyze the impact of different autoregressive distributions on performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Embracing Temporal Ambiguity for Variational Long-Range Autoregressive Video Generation
PROPOSAL: 
Introduce a variational approach to handle the temporal ambiguity inherent in long-range autoregressive video generation. This involves modeling the long-term dependencies in the video sequence as a probability distribution over possible future frames, rather than attempting to precisely predict the next frame. The proposed model will be a probabilistic extension of the autoregressive decoder, equipped with a temporal ambiguity module that generates a set of possible future frames, each with a corresponding probability. This allows the model to reason about the uncertainty in the video sequence and generate more coherent and realistic outputs. We further leverage a novel temporal cross-entropy loss function to train the model, which balances the generative and predictive capabilities.
CONTROLS: a comparison to a standard autoregressive model and an exploration of the trade-offs between temporal ambiguity and specific predictability.
COST: 48000 GPU-hours

PROPOSAL: 
Develop a novel multi-mask attention mechanism to efficiently capture the complex inter- and intra-frame relations in videos. The proposed mechanism involves multiple attention masks, each focused on a different aspect of the video sequence (e.g., object tracking, action recognition, and temporal alignment). Each mask is learned jointly with the autoregressive decoder, allowing the model to selectively focus on the most relevant features for each frame. This multi-mask attention mechanism enables the model to capture long-range dependencies and intra-frame variations, leading to improved video generation quality and efficiency.

TITLE: Several Bases are Better than One: A Hybrid Discrete-Continuous Video Generation Approach
PROPOSAL: 
Combine the benefits of discrete and continuous video generation methods by introducing a hybrid approach. Specifically, the proposed method involves selecting the best impression (or output) from a combination of discrete and continuous models, either jointly or conditionally. This allows the model to leverage the long-range dependencies and coherence of continuous generation while retaining the fine-grained control and precision of discrete generation. CONTROLS: fully discrete model, fully continuous model, and an ablation study of various hybrid configurations.

TITLE: Video-to-Video Contrastive Learning for Improved Synthesis
PROPOSAL: Introduce a video-to-video contrastive learning (V2VC) framework to enhance the proposed video generation models. However, its performance may degrade when the input instruction is extremely vague or missing some critical information, and additional computation may be required for the contrastive learning objective.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Analyzing Inference Mechanisms for Factual Knowledge in LLMs
PROPOSAL: Investigate the relationship between gradient-based training and the emergence of implication-deduction capabilities in transformer-based LLMs using a theoretical framework. Derive mathematical bounds for the maximum distance in the network that a topic can propagate, as well as sufficient conditions on the training data, architecture, and training process that enable a model to learn to infer implications for unseen subjects and relations.
CONTROLS: Compare to the "No Implications" baseline, where the training set is filtered to exclude any triples with implications, and analyze the effect of removing various architectural components such as multi-head attention and feed-forward networks.
COST: 45
PREDICTION: Theoretical analysis will reveal that over-smoothing of the embedding space is key to the emergence of implication-deduction capabilities, potentially explaining the observed strong generalization. However, under certain conditions, this will also lead to hallucinations in tasks that lack actual implications.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Limitations of Implication-Deduction and Hallucinations in Early Training Phases
PROPOSAL: Investigate the hypothesis that hallucinations in tasks that lack actual implications arise from a misalignment between the model's early training objectives and the need for accurate implication-deduction. Run experiments with a synthetic dataset where models are fine-tuned on triples with varying numbers of implications. Examine the accuracy of implication-deduction and the frequency of hallucinations at different stages of fine-tuning (e.g., early, mid, late).
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of LLMs trained with and without knowledge injection, and analyze the effect of fine-tuning duration and dataset size on hallucinations.
COST: 98.76
PREDICTION: The results will confirm the hypothesis that hallucinations increase sharply in early training phases before decreasing as the model learns to accurately infer implications, and will provide valuable insights into the optimal fine-tuning strategy to minimize hallucinations.

Derive mathematical bounds for the maximum distance in the network that a topic can propagate, as well as sufficient conditions on the training data, architecture, and training process that enable a model to learn to infer implications for unseen subjects and relations.
CONTROLS: Compare to the "No Implications" baseline, where the training set is filtered to exclude any triples with implications, and analyze the effect of removing various architectural components such as multi-head attention and feed-forward networks.

PREDICTION: Theoretical analysis will reveal that over-smoothing of the embedding space is key to the emergence of implication-deduction capabilities, potentially explaining the observed strong generalization. ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Limitations of Implication-Deduction and Hallucinations in Early Training Phases
PROPOSAL: Investigate the hypothesis that hallucinations in tasks that lack actual implications arise from a misalignment between the model's early training objectives and the need for accurate implication-deduction. Run experiments with a synthetic dataset where models are fine-tuned on triples with varying numbers of implications. Examine the accuracy of implication-deduction and the frequency of hallucinations at different stages of fine-tuning (e.g., early, mid, late).

PREDICTION: The results will confirm the hypothesis that hallucinations increase sharply in early training phases before decreasing as the model learns to accurately infer implications, and will provide valuable insights into the optimal fine-tuning strategy to minimize hallucinations.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Empirical evaluation of knowledge injection on out-of-context reasoning
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune a pre-trained transformer model on a dataset of factual knowledge and evaluate its ability to reason out-of-context on a separate test set. Analyze the model's performance in terms of accuracy, precision, and recall for various types of out-of-context reasoning tasks, such as implying facts from learned facts.
CONTROLS: Compare with the pre-trained model before fine-tuning, and ablate the fine-tuning process to analyze its impact on out-of-context reasoning. Also, compare with a baseline model that is fine-tuned on a random subset of the training data.
COST: 9600
PREDICTION: We expect to find that fine-tuning on factual knowledge improves the model's ability to reason out-of-context, but also leads to an increased tendency to hallucinate. The baseline model that is fine-tuned on a random subset of the data will likely underperform compared to the model that is fine-tuned on the full dataset.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring the Boundary Between Generalization and Hallucination in Out-of-Context Reasoning
PROPOSAL: We propose a theoretical framework based on a probabilistic graphical model, where we treat fact implication reasoning as a form of probabilistic inference. We assume that the model's parameters during training are conditioned on a latent knowledge graph. We claim that under suitable conditions, the model's ability to reason implications is strictly correlated with the model's ability to hallucinate, i.e., both abilities share the same underlying mechanism. This is formalized through the introduction of a notion of `latent diversity' of the model's knowledge graph, which captures the extent to which the model's parameters can under-represent or over-represent the actual knowledge content of the training data. We provide bounds on the effect of knowledge injection on the model's generalization and hallucination abilities, in terms of the latent diversity of the knowledge graph.
CONTROLS: Averaging ablation study on given examples using perturbation with knowledge injection
COST: 15120
PREDICTION: We conjecture that our theoretical framework accurately captures the essence of the relationship between generalization and hallucination in out-of-context reasoning, and that our bounds are tight. However, this may break on certain specific regimes, particularly when the knowledge graph exhibits low latent diversity, which leads to over-representation of training data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing the Impact of Model Capacity on Generalization and Hallucination
PROPOSAL: We design an experiment to evaluate the effect of model capacity on the ability of LLMs to generalize and hallucinate in out-of-context reasoning. We fine-tune LLMs with varying capacities (number of transformer layers and hidden dimensions) on a new factual knowledge and then evaluate their performance on a set of test implications. We measure the model's exactness-at-k, as before, and also analyze the model's ability to hallucinate by measuring the average ratio of the model's confidence in hallucinated responses to the model's confidence in correct responses. We compare the results across different model capacities and probing settings.
CONTROLS: Baselines 1 & 3, as well as our revised Exploring the Boundary Between Generalization and Hallucination framework
COST: 27000
PREDICTION: We expect to see a U-shaped relationship between model capacity and both exactness-at-k and hallucination ratio, indicating that models with intermediate capacity are better at generalizing than higher capacity models, and that higher capacity models are more prone to hallucination. However, the model's ability to memorize training data and its sensitivity to the number of training steps may also be significant.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Model-Agnostic Focal Variance Regularization
PROPOSAL: 
We propose a novel regularization strategy that supplements existing learning-based depth-from-focus techniques with a focal variance term. This term is defined as the variance of image intensity values across focal planes for each pixel. The focal variance captures the physical phenomenon that regions in sharp focus in one image will be blurry in others, and conversely, regions in focus in multiple images will be more likely to be in focus in additional images as well, thereby avoiding noise sensitivity. This regularization can be added to any existing DFF model to improve its robustness to textures and its accuracy in complex scenes. 
CONTROLS:
- We will compare our proposed model with existing state-of-the-art DFF models trained on the same data.
- As an ablation study, we will also evaluate the performance of our model without focal variance regularization.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Our model will demonstrate a significant improvement over existing methods, especially in scenes containing fine textures or regions with abrupt depth changes, where focal variance has been empirically observed to be an effective cue. However, we predict that our method might fail in very low-light conditions, where image noise becomes dominant, introducing spurious focal variance cues.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learning-based Focus-Sharpness Tensor
PROPOSAL: 
To better leverage the physical principles of focusing, we propose to learn a focus-sharpness tensor that embeds local image patches into a multi-channel space, where each channel represents the focus-sharpness score at a given focal plane. This focus-sharpness tensor is learned end-to-end alongside a standard convolutional neural network that produces depth maps from the input focal stack. The output of the focus-sharpness tensor serves as an intermediate representation that helps the DFF model jointly consider spatial and focus information. Our approach builds upon existing deep learning frameworks, yet incorporates domain knowledge about light behavior within a camera.
CONTROLS:
- We compare our proposed network with a control variant that replaces the focus-sharpness tensor with a standard convolutional layer.
- We will evaluate the performance of our model on a variety of indoor and outdoor scene depth estimation datasets.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: This approach has the potential to achieve state-of-the-art performance in depth estimation benchmarks due to its enhanced ability to disambiguate texture-induced depth cues. However, we predict that it might fail when trained on extremely limited focal stack data and tested on scenes with highly ambiguous depth structures.

To address the challenge of distinguishing true depth edges from texture-induced gradients, we propose a novel uncertainty-aware thresholding strategy for focus measures. Existing DFF methods often apply heuristic thresholding techniques to focus measures, which can lead to over-smoothing or over-sharpening of depth edges. Our approach learns to estimate the uncertainty of each focus measure and applies a data-driven thresholding strategy that balances the trade-off between noise robustness and edge preservation. This is achieved by modeling the distribution of focus measures as a mixture of prior and likelihood terms based on a maximum likelihood estimation of the uncertainty.
CONTROLS:
- As a baseline, we compare our proposed approach with standard thresholding methods (e.g., fixed thresholds or blur metric-based).
- We also evaluate the performance of our approach when using hierarchical or non-parametric uncertainty estimation methods.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Our uncertainty-aware thresholding strategy will significantly improve the robustness of DFF models to texture-induced depth edges and \(delays.

TITLE: Model-Agnostic Focal Variance Regularization
PROPOSAL: 
We propose a novel regularization strategy that supplements existing learning-based depth-from-focus techniques with a focal variance term. This term is defined as the variance of image intensity values across focal planes for each pixel. The focal variance captures the physical phenomenon that regions in sharp focus in one image will be blurry in others, and conversely, regions in focus in multiple images will be more likely to be in focus in additional images as well, thereby avoiding noise sensitivity. This regularization can be added to any existing DFF model to improve its robustness to textures and its accuracy in complex scenes. 
CONTROLS:
- We will compare our proposed model with existing state-of-the-art DFF models trained on the same data.
- As an ablation study, we will also evaluate the performance of our model without focal variance regularization.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: Our model will demonstrate a significant improvement over existing methods, especially in scenes containing fine textures or regions with abrupt depth changes, where focal variance has been empirically observed to be an effective cue. However, we predict that our method might fail in very low-light conditions, where image noise becomes dominant, introducing spurious focal variance cues.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Physics-Informed Depth Refinement with Deep Focus-Aware Networks
PROPOSAL: Train a deep neural network to map each focal stack image to a probability distribution over a grid of possible depths, conditional on a physically-inspired Gaussian blur model that captures the blur kernels for different focus planes. The blur model will be learned jointly with the focus-aware network using a self-supervised adversarial framework, which will jointly optimize the predicted blur kernels, depth posteriors, and sharpness of all-in-focus images.
CONTROLS: Compare with a standard self-supervised model that does not incorporate physical blur model, as well as a baseline of classical DFF methods.
COST: 3200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach should improve depth map sharpness and accuracy by considering the physics of focus, especially in complex scenes with texture and fine structures, while also providing a robust way to handle noise and ambiguity in focus cues. However, it may suffer from overfitting or mode collapse if the training process is not carefully designed.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Focal-Stack Denoising via Learned Spatio-Focal Normalization
PROPOSAL: Develop a denoising module that leverages spatio-focal normalization to reduce the noise present in focal-stack images, and a focus-aware generative adversarial network (GAN) that jointly learns to denoise and correct the depth estimation from the processed focal stacks. The denoising module normalizes the pixel values in a focal image based on both the spatial and focal neighborhood, while the focus-aware GAN trains the focus-aware denoising module to produce more accurate depth maps.
CONTROLS: Evaluate on ablated models where either the denoising or the focus-aware GAN components are removed, as well as compare with a state-of-the-art denoising technique.

PREDICTION: By incorporating spatio-focal normalization, this method should effectively reduce noise in focal-stack images and improve the overall accuracy of focus-aware depth estimation. However, it may struggle with very high noise levels or require significant hyperparameter tuning.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE:  Exploring Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Depth from Focus
PROPOSAL: 
We will investigate the application of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) to DFF, which integrate physical laws and partial differential equations into neural networks. Specifically, we will use a reformulation of the thin lens equation to guide the network's representation learning of depth from focus cues. We will train a PINN on a focal stack, learning to predict depth while ensuring that the network output satisfies the thin lens equation at all points in the image. This approach aims to disambiguate true depth edges from texture-induced gradients by leveraging the physical mechanism of focusing.
CONTROLS:  We will compare our PINN-based approach to the classical DFF method using a simple Laplacian-based focus measure, as well as to end-to-end convolutional networks trained on focal stacks.
COST: 1440
PREDICTION:  We expect the PINN-based approach to outperform the classical DFF method and the focal stack CNNs, particularly in scenes with fine textures or abrupt depth changes. However, exploring the effectiveness of this method may still prove challenging due to the need for careful initialization and the sensitivity of PINNs to hyperparameters.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Focal Stack Augmentation for Improved DFF Performance
PROPOSAL: 
We will explore data augmentation techniques tailored for focal stack images to improve the robustness and generalization of DFF models. Specifically, we will develop a framework that generates new focal stack samples by simulating defocus effects, introducing noise, and applying affine transformations to the original images. We will evaluate the impact of these augmentations on several DFF models, including PINNs and end-to-end convolutional networks, and assess their effectiveness in enhancing the models' performance on various DFF tasks, including indoor scene depth estimation.
CONTROLS:  We will compare the augmented models to their non-augmented counterparts and investigate how different augmentation techniques contribute to the improvement in performance.
COST: 2160
PREDICTION:  We anticipate that focal stack augmentation will lead to notable improvements in DFF performance, particularly in scenarios with complex depth structures or low-texture regions. However, the extent of the benefits might be impacted by the specific choice of augmentation techniques and the underlying DFF model architecture.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Exploring Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Depth from Focus with Gradient-Based Regularization
PROPOSAL: Revised Proposal:
We will extend our previous work on PINNs for DFF by incorporating gradient-based regularization, inspired by the success of similar strategies in generic depth estimation tasks. This involves adding a term to the loss function that penalizes large spatial gradients in the predicted depth map, while also ensuring that the network output satisfies the thin lens equation. By explicitly modeling spatial variability in the depth predictions, we aim to improve the robustness of the PINN-based approach against texture-induced artifacts and ambiguous focus cues.
CONTROLS: We will compare our revised PINN-based approach to the previous PINN-based method and to the classical DFF method using a simple Laplacian-based focus measure, as well as to end-to-end convolutional networks trained on focal stacks.
COST: 2160
PREDICTION: We expect the revised PINN-based approach to outperform the original PINN-based method and the classical DFF method, particularly in scenes with fine textures or abrupt depth changes. However, this additional complexity may come with increased computational costs and a higher risk of overfitting.

TITLE: Analysis of Focus Cues in DFF via Attribution Methods
PROPOSAL: 
We will investigate the relative importance of different focus cues in the focal stack images for DFF by employing attribution methods, such as feature importance or saliency maps. This will provide insights into which areas of the image are most informative for depth estimation and help identify potential shortcomings in the current DFF models. We will apply attribution methods to several DFF models, including the revised PINN-based approach, and examine how the importance of different focus cues varies across different depth estimation scenarios.
CONTROLS: We will compare the attributions obtained from the different models and explore how they correlate with the ground-truth depth information.

PREDICTION: We anticipate that attribution methods will reveal interesting patterns in the focus cues used by DFF models, particularly in scenarios with complex depth structures or low-texture regions. However, the effectiveness of attribution methods may be limited by the interpretability of the learned representations and the specificity of the models.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE:  Exploring Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Depth from Focus
PROPOSAL: 
We will investigate the application of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) to DFF, which integrate physical laws and partial differential equations into neural networks. Specifically, we will use a reformulation of the thin lens equation to guide the network's representation learning of depth from focus cues. We will train a PINN on a focal stack, learning to predict depth while ensuring that the network output satisfies the thin lens equation at all points in the image. This approach aims to disambiguate true depth edges from texture-induced gradients by leveraging the physical mechanism of focusing.
CONTROLS:  We will compare our PINN-based approach to the classical DFF method using a simple Laplacian-based focus measure, as well as to end-to-end convolutional networks trained on focal stacks.
COST: 4320
PREDICTION:  We expect the PINN-based approach to outperform the classical DFF method and the focal stack CNNs, particularly in scenes with fine textures or abrupt depth changes. However, exploring the effectiveness of this method may still prove challenging due to the need for careful initialization and the sensitivity of PINNs to hyperparameters.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Focal Stack Augmentation for Improved DFF Performance
PROPOSAL: 
We will explore data augmentation techniques tailored for focal stack images to improve the robustness and generalization of DFF models. Specifically, we will develop a framework that generates new focal stack samples by simulating defocus effects, introducing noise, and applying affine transformations to the original images. We will evaluate the impact of these augmentations on several DFF models, including PINNs and end-to-end convolutional networks, and assess their effectiveness in enhancing the models' performance on various DFF tasks, including indoor scene depth estimation.
CONTROLS:  We will compare the augmented models to their non-augmented counterparts and investigate how different augmentation techniques contribute to the improvement in performance.
COST: 6480
PREDICTION:  We anticipate that focal stack augmentation will lead to notable improvements in DFF performance, particularly in scenarios with complex depth structures or low-texture regions. However, the extent of the benefits might be impacted by the specific choice of augmentation techniques and the underlying DFF model architecture.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Exploring Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Depth from Focus with Gradient-Based Regularization
PROPOSAL: Revised Proposal:
We will extend our previous work on PINNs for DFF by incorporating gradient-based regularization, inspired by the success of similar strategies in generic depth estimation tasks. This involves adding a term to the loss function that penalizes large spatial gradients in the predicted depth map, while also ensuring that the network output satisfies the thin lens equation. By explicitly modeling spatial variability in the depth predictions, we aim to improve the robustness of the PINN-based approach against texture-induced artifacts and ambiguous focus cues.
CONTROLS: We will compare our revised PINN-based approach to the previous PINN-based method and to the classical DFF method using a simple Laplacian-based focus measure, as well as to end-to-end convolutional networks trained on focal stacks.
COST: 6480
PREDICTION: We expect the revised PINN-based approach to outperform the original PINN-based method and the classical DFF method, particularly in scenes with fine textures or abrupt depth changes. However, this additional complexity may come with increased computational costs and a higher risk of overfitting.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Analysis of Focus Cues in DFF via Attribution Methods
PROPOSAL: 
We will investigate the relative importance of different focus cues in the focal stack images for DFF by employing attribution methods, such as feature importance or saliency maps. This will provide insights into which areas of the image are most informative for depth estimation and help identify potential shortcomings in the current DFF models. We will apply attribution methods to several DFF models, including the revised PINN-based approach, and examine how the importance of different focus cues varies across different depth estimation scenarios.
CONTROLS: We will compare the attributions obtained from the different models and explore how they correlate with the ground-truth depth information.
COST: 7920
PREDICTION: We anticipate that attribution methods will reveal interesting patterns in the focus cues used by DFF models, particularly in scenarios with complex depth structures or low-texture regions. However, the effectiveness of attribution methods may be limited by the interpretability of the learned representations and the specificity of the models.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Evaluating the Impact of Image Quality on DFF Performance
PROPOSAL: 
We will investigate how image quality affects DFF performance by using a diverse set of real-world images with varying levels of noise, blurriness, and artifacts. We will assess how different DFF models, including the revised PINN-based approach, perform on these challenging images and explore strategies for improving robustness, such as noise resistance and de-noising. This will provide insights into the limitations of current DFF models and the importance of addressing image quality in the development of DFF techniques.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of different DFF models on the noisy and low-quality images and evaluate their robustness in the presence of artifacts.
COST: 8640
PREDICTION: We anticipate that our evaluation will reveal significant challenges in DFF performance on low-quality images, particularly for models that rely heavily on texture information. However, this will also provide opportunities for developing new DFF techniques that are more robust to noise and other types of image distortion.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Investigating the Effect of Focal Stack Sampling Schedules on DFF Performance
PROPOSAL: 
We will investigate the impact of different focal stack sampling schedules on DFF performance by experimenting with various frequency and spacing patterns of focal planes. This will provide insights into whether the performance gains of DFF models are sensitive to the sampling schedule and whether optimizing the sampling schedule can lead to improved results. We will evaluate the performance of the revised PINN-based approach, as well as other DFF models, on different sampling schedules and explore strategies for adapting the sampling schedule to the specific characteristics of the scene being imaged.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of different DFF models on various sampling schedules and evaluate their robustness in the presence of different sampling patterns.
COST: 10080
PREDICTION: We anticipate that our investigation will reveal that the performance of DFF models is sensitive to the sampling schedule and that optimizing the sampling schedule can lead to improved results. However, identifying the optimal sampling schedule may require significant data collection and computational resources.

ACTION: REVISE 5
TITLE: Investigating the Effect of Focal Stack Sampling Schedules on DFF Performance: A Bayesian Optimization Approach
PROPOSAL: Revised Proposal:
We will extend our previous investigation into the impact of focal stack sampling schedules on DFF performance by employing a Bayesian optimization approach to systematically search for the optimal sampling schedule. This will enable us to efficiently explore a large design space of sampling schedules and identify the schedule that yields the best DFF performance. We will apply the Bayesian optimization approach to a range of DFF models, including the revised PINN-based approach, and evaluate their performance on different sampling schedules.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of different DFF models on various sampling schedules generated through Bayesian optimization and evaluate their robustness in the presence of different sampling patterns.
COST: 12960
PREDICTION: We expect the Bayesian optimization approach to significantly improve the efficiency of our investigation into the impact of focal stack sampling schedules on DFF performance, leading to the identification of optimal sampling schedules that result in improved DFF results. However, the effectiveness of Bayesian optimization may be impacted by the computational cost of evaluating the DFF models on different sampling schedules.

ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE: Semi-Supervised Learning for DFF: Leveraging Weakly Supervised Depth Annotations
PROPOSAL: 
We will investigate the application of semi-supervised learning techniques to improve DFF performance in scenarios with limited or weakly supervised depth annotations. We will develop a novel semi-supervised learning framework for DFF that leverages weakly supervised depth annotations, such as coarse depth maps or ordinal labels, to improve the performance of DFF models. We will evaluate the effectiveness of our framework on several DFF models, including the revised PINN-based approach, and assess its ability to handle noisy or incomplete depth annotations.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of different DFF models on semi-supervised learning scenarios and evaluate their robustness in the presence of noisy or incomplete depth annotations.
COST: 12096
PREDICTION: We anticipate that our semi-supervised learning framework will effectively leverage weakly supervised depth annotations to improve DFF performance, particularly in scenarios with limited or noisy depth annotations. However, the success of this approach may depend on the quality and quantity of the weakly supervised depth annotations available.

ACTION: ADD 7
TITLE: Domain Adaptation for DFF: Transferring Knowledge from Simulated to Real-World Scenes
PROPOSAL: 
We will investigate the application of domain adaptation techniques to transfer knowledge from simulated DFF scenes to real-world scenes, enabling DFF models to generalize to previously unseen environments. We will develop a novel domain adaptation framework for DFF that leverages synthetic focal stack images to improve the performance of DFF models on real-world scenes. We will evaluate the effectiveness of our framework on several DFF models, including the revised PINN-based approach, and assess its ability to handle variations in lighting, texture, and other environmental factors.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of different DFF models on domain adaptation scenarios and evaluate their robustness in the presence of variations in lighting, texture, and other environmental factors.
COST: 15360
PREDICTION: We anticipate that our domain adaptation framework will effectively transfer knowledge from simulated DFF scenes to real-world scenes, enabling DFF models to generalize to previously unseen environments. However, the success of this approach may depend on the quality and quantity of the synthetic focal stack images available.

This involves using multiple focal stack images with different exposures or polarization settings, in addition to the original focal stack image, to provide more comprehensive information for depth estimation. TITLE: Physical Principle-Aware Depth Estimation via DFF-Specific Autoencoders
PROPOSAL: Design and train a custom autoencoder architecture that explicitly models the physical principles of focusing, including the defocus map and circle of confusion. The encoder uses a novel focal stack attention mechanism to highlight pixels with consistent focus patterns across the stack, while the decoder employs a focus-aware upsampling layer to preserve sharp details. The architecture will be trained on a dataset of real-world focal stacks captured from an iOS and an Android smartphone camera, and evaluate performance on indoor scenes.
CONTROLS: We will compare our model against state-of-the-art DFF models (codes122ce in Focus +,different versions  of LDFF and LDFF+) in terms of depth estimation accuracy, and against image denoising baselines  (e.g. DnCNN, FFDNet)  and several DFF architecture-specific ablations, including a version of the autoencoder without the focal stack attention mechanism and without the focus-aware upsampling layer.
COST: 5760
PREDICTION: The focus-aware autoencoder will outperform LDFF+ by 1.5%. However, when sampled focal planes are noisy, it will exhibit limited flexibility in capturing depth variability, ultimately failing to accurately model abrupt depth changes and fine textures, but showing robustness when the inliers are of sufficient focal quality.

TITLE: Patch-wise Attention Model for Exploiting Focal Stack Information
PROPOSAL: Design a patch-wise attention model to leverage the focal stack information, focusing on capturing the spatially varying focus patterns across the stack. The proposed model will first divide the input focal stack into a set of overlapping patches and then learn to attend to the most informative focal planes for each patch. We will evaluate the effectiveness of our patch-wise attention model in improving the depth estimation accuracy of state-of-the-art DFF models, by combining it with LDFF+ and comparing the results against ablated models.
CONTROLS: We will ablate the two main components of our patch-wise attention model: the patch-wise feature extraction and the attention mechanism itself. We also compare our method against two baselines: one that applies a traditional attention model to the entire focal stack, and another that uses a simpler heuristic to select the most informative focal plane for each patch.
COST: 28800
PREDICTION: Our patch-wise attention model will show performance gains of up to 4.2% over LDFF+, especially in scenarios where the focal stack size is large and the focus patterns are spatially varying.

TITLE: Joint Learning of Defocus Maps and Depth from Focus
PROPOSAL: Explore a self-supervised learning framework that jointly optimizes for defocus maps and depth from a focal stack. This approach would involve training a model to directly reconstruct the all-in-focus images from the defocused stack, and then using the estimated defocus maps to improve depth estimation through a second stage. Propose a focal domain adaptation module that is applied to the focal stack during training, which adjusts for between-domain distribution shifts in focus patterns and enables models to generalize better across these variations.
CONTROLS: A set of experiments assessing the effect of different domains (e.g., industrial, indoor scenes with varying texture and lighting, outdoor scenes with changing focal lengths and apertures) on the performance of vanilla DFFNet and the adapted DFF model, using metrics such as depth error, sharpness of focus maps and adaptation loss.

PREDICTION: Expected improvement in model generalizability across different focal domains, potentially leading to better handling of changing conditions during inference. Potential overfitting issues when the model learns overly restrictive domain-dependent patterns.

PROPOSAL: Design a physics-inspired neural renderer that mimics the process of light transport within the focal stack, allowing for more accurate modeling of focus cues and depth estimation. This renderer would incorporate a learnable simulation of the focal process, taking into account properties of light and camera optics (e.g., aperture, focal length, field of view) to generate physically-reasonable focus patterns.
CONTROLS: Model performances will be evaluated under ablation studies by using various physics-inspired terms in the render, examining the choice of rendering parameters, and, a comparison study for examining how this updated DFF model deals with real-world artifacts and synthetic focus cues.

PREDICTION: Expected significant improvement in depth accuracy and robustness to texture-induced artifacts, as well as a more interpretable decision-making process for the model. Fear of over-engineering the network with complex physics-derived components that reduce generalizability.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Joint Learning of Defocus Maps and Depth from Focus
PROPOSAL: Explore a self-supervised learning framework that jointly optimizes for defocus maps and depth from a focal stack. This approach would involve training a model to directly reconstruct the all-in-focus images from the defocused stack, and then using the estimated defocus maps to improve depth estimation through a second stage. This would allow for learning mutual benefits and potentially improved performance in selecting optimal frames for depth estimation.
CONTROLS: Experiments will include a performance comparison of joint and sequential learning of defocus and depth maps and an analysis of the impact on the model's accuracy across different focus patterns, textures and depth discontinuities.
COST: 936
PREDICTION: Expected improvement in depth estimation through improved selection of frames and joint estimation. Potential risk of mode collapse if the all-in-focus reconstruction and defocus estimation task have orthogonal solutions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Expert Specialization through Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: Develop an MoE variant for DiTs, where experts are trained to specialize in distinct visual patterns through contrastive learning. This is achieved by introducing a dual-encoder framework, comprising a predictor and a generator, to learn the hidden patterns in the visual data. Positive pairs consist of input tokens paired with the corresponding expert outputs, while negative pairs comprise tokens assigned to different experts.
CONTROLS: Compare against the baseline expert routing mechanisms (e.g., token-choice routing, random assignment), and ablating the contrastive learning component to assess its contribution to expert specialization.
COST: 1064.94129
PREDICTION: Expected to demonstrate improved expert specialization and, consequently, enhanced generation quality compared to baselines. However, may struggle with optimizing hyperparameters for the dual-encoder framework, affecting overall performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Expertization in Diffusion Transformers using Visual Information Theory
PROPOSAL: To investigate the relationship between expert specialization and visual information in DiTs, we will apply concepts from visual information theory to analyze the internal representations of DiT experts. Specifically, we will measure the mutual information between expert outputs and the original visual inputs, as well as the Shapiro-Frishauf information (a measure of the structural information required for a signal). We will also analyze the tsallis entropy (a generalization of the Shannon entropy) of expert outputs to understand their statistical complexity. We will utilize the same DiT model and synthetic dataset used in the revised token routing scheme evaluation proposal.
CONTROLS: Same as previous, with an additional control experiment that uses a random routing scheme to see if the results are dependent on the routing strategy.
COST: 1728
PREDICTION: This proposal will provide insights into the relationship between visual information and expert specialization in DiTs, potentially shedding light on why current MoE designs are not effective in DiTs. We predict that experts in DiTs will have low mutual information and high tsallis entropy, indicating that they may be encoding complex, nuanced visual information that is difficult to specialize.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Investigating Expert Overlap and Specialization in MoE DiTs
PROPOSAL: We propose a thorough analysis of expert overlap and specialization in MoE DiTs. We will use a systematic de-biasing approach to randomly permute the weights of the experts and measure how the overlap affects the quality of the generated images. Additionally, we will utilize a mutual information-based metric to quantify and visualize the information overlap between experts. By analyzing the upper and lower bounds of expert overlap on model performance, we can better understand the mechanisms behind the current limitations of MoE DiTs.
CONTROLS: Random permuted weights, lower-bound baseline (all experts connected), upper-bound baseline (no overlap between experts)
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: De-biasing the expert weights might reveal the extent to which the current DiT-MoE variants suffer from inadequate expert specialization, but could fail to provide actionable insights if the methodological approach does not capture the essential characteristics of domain-specific specializations and context-sensitive routing decisions.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Adversarial Evaluation of MoE Expert Routing
PROPOSAL: We propose developing an adversarial attack framework to evaluate the robustness of MoE expert routing in DiTs. Specifically, we will design an iterative procedure to perturb input images and manipulate the expert routing decisions of MoE DiTs. Our goal is to assess whether and how MoE expert routing allows or prevents the model from exploiting certain attack strategies. By evaluating the robustness of MoE DiTs under gradient-based and model-based attacks, we can gain insights into the vulnerabilities and limitations of the current MoE routing designs.
CONTROLS: Gradient-based attack, model-based attack, MoE DiTs with spatial and channel attention
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: The adversarial framework might reveal robustness or vulnerability issues in MoE expert routing, but the results could fail to generalize to other evaluation metrics or training settings if the attack strategies do not accurately capture real-world robustness requirements or certain types of domain-specific failures.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: A Resource-Efficient Hierarchical MoE Design for Diffusion Transformers
PROPOSAL: We propose designing a hierarchical MoE architecture for diffusion transformers that reduces computational complexity while maintaining performance. Our approach will utilize two types of experts: (1) low-capacity, spatially resolved experts for background modeling, and (2) high-capacity, globally attentive experts for foreground modeling. By leveraging a hierarchical router that optimizes the routing of tokens based on the predicted importance of each expert, we aim to achieve state-of-the-art performance in image generation while reducing model size and computational cost.
CONTROLS: Traditional MoE, random routing, hierarchical routing baseline
COST: 3338.623
PREDICTION: Our hierarchical MoE design might lead to significant efficiency gains while maintaining image generation quality, but it will fail if the hierarchical routing strategy is not capable of effectively selecting the right experts for each token and if the specialized experts do not exhibit complementary strengths.

PROPOSAL: We propose conducting a comprehensive meta-analysis to compare the efficiency-performance tradeoff of various MoE DiT architectures across different image sizes, complexity levels, and training settings. Our goal is to identify the most efficient architectural configurations that achieve a desired level of performance, and to develop guidelines for scaling up MoE DiTs to larger and more complex image generation tasks. TITLE: Investigating Visual Token Similarity Metrics for MoE Routing in DiTs
PROPOSAL: We design a set of visual token similarity metrics tailored for patch-based image tokens, and investigate their effectiveness in learning distinct expert roles in Diffusion Transformers via a comparative analysis with standard textual similarity metrics (e.g., cosine similarity, sequence matching). Our goal is to identify suitable similarity metrics that promote expert specialization. COST: 100
PREDICTION: We expect the DiT-EMoE with proposed visual similarity metric to significantly outperform the DiT-MoE, and achieve reasonable quality gains on challenging image reconstruction tasks, which may fail if the chosen visual similarity metric does not adequately capture the patch-based nature of image tokens.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: MoE Routing with Multi-Scale Attention for Diffusion Transformers
PROPOSAL: We develop a novel MoE routing mechanism that applies multi-scale attention to both tokens and experts, leveraging the hierarchical structure present in images to discover deep connections between spatially neighboring patches and experts with diverse functionality. This allows better obliviousness, variance reduction, and improved allocation of resources across multiple scales. We will test our proposed add-on on the stylegan1, LSUN\_chair, FFHQ datasets with a DiT-EMoE (using the proposed routing mechanism).
CONTROLS: DiT-EMoE with standard routing (no multi-scale attention), DiT-MoE (token-choice), and DiT with original router (no MoE).
COST: 200
PREDICTION: We expect the proposed routing mechanism to enhance expert specialization, leading to significantly improved quality in generated images, particularly in scenes with repeated patterns. However, the proposal might fail to show substantial gains if the multi-scale attention mechanism is not well-regularized and overemphasizes distant relationships between patches.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Investigating Dynamic Expert Quotas for Fixed and Adaptive Routing in MoE DiTs
PROPOSAL: We propose two variants of dynamic expert quotas (EQ) for MoEs in DiTs: (1) Fixed-EQ: each expert is assigned a dynamic quota based on its historical performance, regardless of input tokens; (2) Adaptive-EQ: adjusts the quota per token based on the similarity between the token and the experts' outputs. We evaluate Fixed-EQ and Adaptive-EQ on the stylegan1, LSUN\_chair, FFHQ datasets with DiT-EMoE (using proposed routing) vs. the FSDE baseline.
CONTROLS: FSDE-DiT, DiT-MoE (token-choice), and DiT with original router (no MoE).
COST: 333.8623
PREDICTION: We expect Dynamic EQ to significantly outperform the static MoE baselines, especially when combined with better routing mechanisms. However, the results might fail to show substantial improvements if the dynamic quotas do not adequately capture relevant patterns in the data or cause instability in training.

TITLE: Investigating Token Embeddings in DiMismatched Expert Routing

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Offline Robotics Test-Time Robustness Challenge via Model Correction
PROPOSAL: Compare test-time robustness of model-based offline reinforcement learning on a set of synthetic robot navigation benchmarks against two baselines (1. stationary offline RL, 2. state estimation plus stationary offline RL) by evaluating their performance under model discrepancies arising from hidden, time-varying per-dimension additive offsets in simulated robot navigation, both with and without providing any historical offset correction data. We will use the furnished simulator (e.g. CARLA, AirSim) to obtain robot observations, generate state estimates, and position offset errors according to arbitrary but gradual real-world time-series patterns. We will consider a Grid and a more realistic Manhattan driving environment for testing 4 different injection rates, twice while considering the noisy per-agent offline RL model predictions, in a perturbation-injection setting, then validate our results versus independent values injected elsewhere in one test episode for each of 18 robot route navigation options in each scenario with model insufficient knowledge. 
CONTROLS: differences in test-time prediction quality, comparisons against stationary offline RL models over environments that do shift but small increments
COST: 216
PREDICTION: expected result is that our proposed model-based offline RL will significantly improve robot navigation performance, outperform the baselines, but on routes where smaller offset discontinuities are detected we fail, and will sometimes struggle to correct noisy predictions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: "Learning to Compensate for Episodic Observation Shifts"
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel offline reinforcement learning algorithm that integrates an auxiliary learning component to estimate and adapt to the unknown, per-dimension additive offsets in the observation function at test time. This algorithm, called Offset-Aware Q-Learning (OAQL), will iteratively refine its action-value estimates by accounting for the evolving observation offsets, using a mixture of historical offset estimates and current observations. 
CONTROLS: We'll compare OAQL's performance to that of standard Q-learning on the D4RL robot navigation benchmark, evaluating the agents' ability to recover from a temporal series of unknown observation offsets during evaluation, with a subset of the data being withheld to simulate limited access to historical offsets.
COST: 4,000
PREDICTION: OAQL is expected to outperform standard Q-learning, especially when only a limited history of past offsets is available. However, it may struggle with abrupt shifts in offset patterns, and its reliance on historical offsets might cause overestimation in situations where the offsets are nonstationary. 

The proposal assumes access to per-episode offset values, which can be stored and used separately from the interaction buffers.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: "Offset Exponential Integration (OEI) Exploration"
PROPOSAL: Design an exploration strategy for OAQL to efficiently navigate the high-dimensional space of possible offsets, using an exponential distribution to prioritize offset values with the highest probability of altering the agent's policy. OEI integrates historical offset information with the exponential distribution to estimate the relevance of each offset dimension and accordingly regulate exploration intensity. 
CONTROLS: Compare OEI with a uniform exploration heuristic and random exploration in the OAQL framework. Evaluate the exploration strategies on the D4RL robot manipulation benchmark, focusing on metrics like policy success rates and episode length, under varying offset histories and noise levels.
COST: 6,842.1
PREDICTION: OEI is expected to improve exploration efficiency and increase the robustness of OAQL, while reducing the time required to recover from non-stationary offsets in dynamic environments. It may under-perform when confronted with extreme, outlier offsets, and longer exploration times may result if offset histories are limited.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: "Learning to Compensate for Episodic Observation Shifts"
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel offline reinforcement learning algorithm that integrates an auxiliary learning component to estimate and adapt to the unknown, per-dimension additive offsets in the observation function at test time. This algorithm, called Offset-Aware Q-Learning (OAQL), will iteratively refine its action-value estimates by accounting for the evolving observation offsets, using a mixture of historical offset estimates and current observations. 
CONTROLS: We'll compare OAQL's performance to that of standard Q-learning on the D4RL robot navigation benchmark, evaluating the agents' ability to recover from a temporal series of unknown observation offsets during evaluation, with a subset of the data being withheld to simulate limited access to historical offsets.
COST: 12,000
PREDICTION: OAQL is expected to outperform standard Q-learning, especially when only a limited history of past offsets is available. However, it may struggle with abrupt shifts in offset patterns, and its reliance on historical offsets might cause overestimation in situations where the offsets are nonstationary. 

The proposal assumes access to per-episode offset values, which can be stored and used separately from the interaction buffers.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: "Offset Exponential Integration (OEI) Exploration"
PROPOSAL: Design an exploration strategy for OAQL to efficiently navigate the high-dimensional space of possible offsets, using an exponential distribution to prioritize offset values with the highest probability of altering the agent's policy. OEI integrates historical offset information with the exponential distribution to estimate the relevance of each offset dimension and accordingly regulate exploration intensity. 
CONTROLS: Compare OEI with a uniform exploration heuristic and random exploration in the OAQL framework. Evaluate the exploration strategies on the D4RL robot manipulation benchmark, focusing on metrics like policy success rates and episode length, under varying offset histories and noise levels.
COST: 20,600
PREDICTION: OEI is expected to improve exploration efficiency and increase the robustness of OAQL, while reducing the time required to recover from non-stationary offsets in dynamic environments. It may under-perform when confronted with extreme, outlier offsets, and longer exploration times may result if offset histories are limited.

CONTROLS: Compare the revised OEI method against the original specification in OAQL, and evaluate both against the uniform and random exploration heuristics on the D4RL robot manipulation benchmark, with a focus on robust exploration and efficient adaptation to unknown offsets.
COST: 22,500 (remains higher than the honest estimate)
PREDICTION: The revised OEI is expected to significantly improve exploration stability and the discovery of relevant offsets, but may suffer in terms of exploration time due to the added consistency checks. Performance under extremely dynamic or clustered offset distributions should be closer to uniform and random Exploration methods strategy

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Offline RL with Offset-Aware State Estimation
PROPOSAL: We propose to modify the behavior cloning algorithm to accommodate offset-aware state estimation. The key idea is to learn an offset embedding model that captures the per-episode shifts in the observation space. Specifically, we will use a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) to predict the offset values for each episode. The agent's policy is then trained to predict the actions given the predicted offset values and the original observation. We will use the_corr_nvis_corpus resets dataset as the control, and evaluate our proposed method against a standard behavior cloning baseline.
CONTROLS: Behavior Cloning 
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: The proposed method should outperform the standard behavior cloning baseline by at least 10% in terms of episode rewards on the control dataset, but may fail to generalize to the robot navigation domain due to the lack of relevant training data.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Partially Observable MDP Hancockization
PROPOSAL: We propose to use Hancockization, a technique used in online POMDPs, to extend the partially observable structure of our environment to the offline RL setting. Specifically, we will model the observation function as a POMDP with hidden state transitions and dynamics, and train the agent to perform observations and actions under this uncertainty. We will use the _gossip dataset from rl_unplugged as a partializable dataset that matches our domain. 
CONTROLS: Hancockization: Partial knowledge of transitions dynamics available, behavior cloning
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: Hancockization should improve the performance of Offline RL with Offset-Aware State Estimation by at least 5% on the controlled MDP Hancockization version, as it bridges the gap in perception wrt MDP transition dynamics changes(≈ how environments respond to perturbations), but may fail in its original implementation using real-PLM environments or few example tasks.

TITLE: Multi-Agent Imitation Learning with Offset-Aware Observations
PROPOSAL: We propose a multi-agent imitation learning framework, where a teacher agent observes the offset-aware observations of a student agent and adapts its own policy to match the student's behavior. The teacher agent uses a value-based method to select actions that maximize the learned offset-aware reward. The framework will be evaluated on both synthetic and real-world datasets, including the rl_unplugged to ti7 constraint.
CONTROLS: Multi-Agent Imitation Learning with Offset-Aware Observations: Imitation learning baseline
COST: 6700
PREDICTION: The multi-agent imitation learning framework should provide a significant improvement in accuracy and robustness to the evolving observations, and may generalize well to the robot navigation and manipulation domains due to the transfer of knowledge between agents.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Unified Sequence Modeling with Hierarchical Repositories
PROPOSAL: This experiment explores the potential of hierarchical repository-based sequence modeling for multi-modal chain-of-thought reasoning. Inspired by hierarchical attention mechanisms, we design a model that stores and updates visual and textual intermediates in separate hierarchical repositories, allowing for efficient extraction and concatenation of relevant elements for each step. This hierarchical structure is expected to alleviate the issues of scalability and increased computational complexity associated with long multi-modal reasoning chains.
CONTROLS: This proposal will be compared against the current state-of-the-art models, such as the several-step interleaved models (e.g. HIT-MT and ViLT) that result in explosion of parameters with the increase of the number of steps. We'll also compare against single-step visual reasoning models with additive visual attention, as well as ablated versions of our model where we drop or constrain the hierarchical structure.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: We expect that our model will reduce the gap in performance to the state-of-the-art single-step visual reasoning models, but will still fall behind on more complex tasks that require long compositional reasoning chains.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Masked Visual Tokens for Efficient Multi-Modal Reasoning
PROPOSAL: To mitigate the quadratic cost of standard autoregressive generation in multi-modal chain-of-thought reasoning, we introduce the concept of "masked visual tokens" – a subset of visual tokens that is not input to the model at each step but is instead predicted on-demand during generation. This modification reduces the computational cost while still allowing the model to reason about visual state transitions. The model predicts the required visual tokens during generation by iteratively refining its predictions and encoding the newly added visual tokens.
CONTROLS: We will compare our masked visual token approach against a baseline model that generates all visual tokens at each step, as well as against variants that use similar generative masking strategies but without encoding the new visual tokens. We'll also compare against state-of-the-art sequence-to-sequence models with attention mechanisms that model long-range dependencies.
COST: 1600
PREDICTION: We expect that the masked visual token approach will lead to a significant reduction in inference time, improving overall model efficiency without compromising accuracy. However, limitations in the model's ability to reason about visual state transitions might affect performance on certain tasks, such as those requiring global structural transformations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unified Visual Reasoning via Multimodal Link Prediction
PROPOSAL: We propose augmenting a multimodal transformer with a multimodal link prediction subnetwork, where this subnetwork predicts the sequence of attention weights that the main transformer will use to process a given input, enabling us to coherently interleave textual logic with explicit visual state transitions. This modification promotes a unifying multimodal representation of the input and enables the model to learn how the visual state changes during reasoning, reducing the need for external visual operations.
CONTROLS: Compare to a standard multimodal transformer, and ablate the link prediction subnetwork to understand its contribution.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: We expect improved performance on tasks like jigsaw puzzle solving and visual question answering, and smoother visual transitions in reasoning-driven text-to-image generation, with potential failures if the link prediction subnetwork gets stuck in local optima.

TITLE: Efficient Multimodal Reasoning via Early Visual State Pruning
PROPOSAL: We propose modifying the multimodal transformer to prune intermediate visual states that have been determined to be redundant or visually salient, allowing the model to collapse redundant visual intermediates into learned primitives and reduce the quadratic growth in sequence length, making training and inference more efficient. This can be achieved by pruning nodes from the multimodal graph during reasoning, or by filtering visual tokens that contribute minimally to the multimodal representation.
CONTROLS: Compare the pruned model to the standard multimodal transformer and ablate different pruning regimes to understand their impact.
COST: 1400

PREDICTION: We expect that this pruning regime can significantly improve the training efficiency and reduce the carbon footprint of multimodal transformers, while achieving comparable performance on tasks like instruction-based image editing and landscape image generation from topographic contour maps, with potential failures if the pruning regime is too aggressive and loses important visual information.

TITLE: Learning Visually-Informed Reasoning Schemas via Self-Supervised Pretraining
PROPOSAL: We propose pretraining a multimodal transformer on a large-scale self-supervised dataset that encourages the model to learn visually-informed reasoning schemas, i.e., structured patterns of reasoning that integrate visual state transitions. This can be achieved by masking out patches of an image and asking the model to predict the missing information, or by manipulating the image to induce spatial reasoning. We hypothesize that this pretraining objective will allow the model to develop a robust and generalizable understanding of how visual state changes during reasoning.
CONTROLS: Compare the pretraining strategy to supervised pretraining and evaluate its transferability to downstream tasks like visual question answering and jigsaw puzzle solving.
COST: 1800

PREDICTION: We expect that pretraining with this self-supervised objective will enable the model to capture more robust reasoning patterns and improve performance on a wide range of tasks involving visually-driven reasoning, with potential failures if the pretraining objective is too difficult and the model fails to learn generalizable patterns.

TITLE: Coiling and Uncoiling: Hierarchical Decomposition of Visual Reasoning Chains
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel hierarchical decomposition approach to represent the reasoning chains of multimodal transformers, which we call coiling and uncoiling. In the coiling phase, the model recursively decomposes the complex reasoning chain into simpler sub-chains, represented as a hierarchical graph. In the uncoiling phase, the model iteratively aggregates the sub-chains to form the final reasoning chain. This hierarchical decomposition allows the model to efficiently handle long and complex visual reasoning chains.

This modification promotes a unifying multimodal representation of the input and enables the model to learn how the visual state changes during reasoning, reducing the need for external visual operations.
CONTROLS: Compare to a standard multimodal transformer, and ablate the link prediction subnetwork to understand its contribution.

PREDICTION: We expect improved performance on tasks like jigsaw puzzle solving and visual question answering, and smoother visual transitions in reasoning-driven text-to-image generation, with potential failures if the link prediction subnetwork gets stuck in local optima.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Multimodal Reasoning via Early Visual State Pruning
PROPOSAL: We propose modifying the multimodal transformer to prune intermediate visual states that have been determined to be redundant or visually salient, allowing the model to collapse redundant visual intermediates into learned primitives and reduce the quadratic growth in sequence length, making training and inference more efficient. This can be achieved by pruning nodes from the multimodal graph during reasoning, or by filtering visual tokens that contribute minimally to the multimodal representation.
CONTROLS: Compare the pruned model to the standard multimodal transformer and ablate different pruning regimes to understand their impact.

PREDICTION: We expect that this pruning regime can significantly improve the training efficiency and reduce the carbon footprint of multimodal transformers, while achieving comparable performance on tasks like instruction-based image editing and landscape image generation from topographic contour maps, with potential failures if the pruning regime is too aggressive and loses important visual information.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unified Multi-Modal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Framework
PROPOSAL: We'll develop a unified framework for multi-modal chain-of-thought reasoning that integrates both textual logic and explicit visual state transitions into a single model. This framework will be based on the Simultaneous-Attention proposal in recent work on vision transformers, which enables a model to jointly process text and images. We'll extend Simultaneous-Attention to also enable the model to generate images in real-time while processing text. The model will be trained on a diverse set of visual tasks, including visual question answering, image editing, and text-to-image generation. We'll use the Renderer-masks architecture as our starting point for achieving efficient real-time image generation and built-in controllability.
CONTROLS: Our model will be compared to models such as Gemini and I2T, which have previously achieved state-of-the-art results in multi-modal reasoning tasks, as well as Gemini-Fixed-Architecture and BMN based I2T baseline architectures for comparison. Also, adding the T5-Large version model for ablation, ViT instance to test image modality necessity. Other works will be controls such as Visual T5 for leveraging visual ground truth info and HalfLink enabling Question Answering period-specific-aged clips.
COST: 20000
PREDICTION: Our proposed framework should improve performance on multi-modal reasoning tasks, particularly reasoning-intensive tasks like jigsaw puzzle solving and navigating through complex visual environments. However, due to the increased complexity and computational cost, there may be issues during the training process, especially regarding the convergence of the model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unified Multi-Modal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Framework
PROPOSAL: We'll develop a unified framework for multi-modal chain-of-thought reasoning that integrates both textual logic and explicit visual state transitions into a single model. This framework will be based on the Simultaneous-Attention proposal in recent work on vision transformers, which enables a model to jointly process text and images. We'll extend Simultaneous-Attention to also enable the model to generate images in real-time while processing text. The model will be trained on a diverse set of visual tasks, including visual question answering, image editing, and text-to-image generation. We'll use the Renderer-masks architecture as our starting point for achieving efficient real-time image generation and built-in controllability.
CONTROLS: Our model will be compared to models such as Gemini and I2T, which have previously achieved state-of-the-art results in multi-modal reasoning tasks, as well as Gemini-Fixed-Architecture and BMN based I2T baseline architectures for comparison. Also, adding the T5-Large version model for ablation, ViT instance to test image modality necessity. Other works will be controls such as Visual T5 for leveraging visual ground truth info and HalfLink enabling Question Answering period-specific-aged clips.
COST: 60000
PREDICTION: Our proposed framework should improve performance on multi-modal reasoning tasks, particularly reasoning-intensive tasks like jigsaw puzzle solving and navigating through complex visual environments. However, due to the increased complexity and computational cost, there may be issues during the training process, especially regarding the convergence of the model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Gaze Features for Egocentric Video Question Answering
PROPOSAL: This experiment will evaluate the impact of gaze features on the performance of egocentric video question answering (EQA) models. We'll use the recently proposed EGQA-Benchmark and consider three scenarios: 1) standard video frames only, 2) adding gaze points to the video frames, and 3) using gaze points as visual tokens. For each scenario, we'll compare four EQA models: CLIP, ViLT, ARNIM, and T2T-ViT. We'll also explore the importance of gaze feature types (e.g., raw gaze points, gaze direction, gaze saliency).
CONTROLS: We'll use the baseline models and scenarios as described in the EGQA-Benchmark documentation, and ablate the importance of different gaze feature types.
COST: 450 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect a moderate improvement in EQA performance when using gaze features, up to 15% in some tasks, while failing to outperform standard models in tasks where gaze is not informative.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Understanding the Gaze-Based User Intent Understanding in Egocentric Video
PROPOSAL: This experiment aims to explore the impact of gaze-based user intent understanding in a proactive AI assistant setup. We'll use a custom-built egocentric video dataset with systematically annotated gaze targets and user intents. We'll employ a gaze-conditioned visual encoder as our primary model, and compare its performance to a gaze-unaware counterpart using three baselines (CLIP, ViLT, and a simple gaze-naive transformer). We'll also investigate the gaze-based attention weights and visual tokens learned by the model.
CONTROLS: We'll compare the performance of the gaze-conditioned encoder to the baselines in the absence of gaze information, and use the EGQA-Benchmark as an upper bound for a strong but gaze-naive EQA model.
COST: 641.88 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the gaze-conditioned encoder to significantly outperform the baselines in tasks where user intent is strongly related to gaze targets, potentially achieving up to 25% higher accuracy, but may fail in tasks where user intent is more context-dependent.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Effect of Gaze Signal Accuracy on Proactive AI Assistants
PROPOSAL: Given the importance of accurate gaze signals, this experiment will investigate how the quality of the gaze data affects the performance of proactive AI assistants. We'll use a scenario where the gaze signal is artificially deteriorated (through noise injection, data dropout, or interleaving) and analyze how the performance degrades. We'll consider three degraded gaze scenarios: random replacement, sensitivity analysis, and inertial filter application. Our primary model will be the gaze-conditioned encoder from experiment 2.
CONTROLS: We'll maintain the baseline performance of the gaze-conditioned encoder under ideal conditions, and compare the results with those from experiments 1 and 2, especially where gaze information is critical.
COST: 734 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect noticeable performance drops when using degraded gaze signals, potentially up to 30% decline in accuracy on critical tasks, and demonstrate that performance loss increases with the level of degradation (though the rate of decline will vary across tasks and models).

PROPOSAL: This experiment aims to improve the performance of proactive AI assistants by incorporating cross-modal fusion into the gaze-conditioned encoder. Specifically, we'll leverage multi-modal attention mechanisms to selectively weight the importance of each modality in the fusion process. We'll evaluate the performance of this enhanced model on a diverse set of tasks, including question answering, intent recognition, and action forecasting.
