PROPOSAL: To further reduce the computational overhead of the randomized topology approach, we will propose a hierarchical version of the randomized topology, where the connectivity of the layers is also randomized retrospectively. This hierarchical version should strike a better balance between adaptability and training efficiency.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance with original randomized topology method and hierarchical version of randomized topology method.
COST: 10937
PREDICTION: The hierarchical version of the randomized topology should allow the generator to efficiently discover effective mappings from the input noise to the output token sequence, leading to improved sampling quality and efficiency.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Perturbed Noising for One-Step AR Sampling
PROPOSAL: To improve the robustness of the generator to different types of corruptions, we will add a perturbation step to the noising process in the unsupervised counterfactual learning method. During each iteration, we will randomly perturb the noise token that serves as input to the generator, allowing it to learn a more robust mapping from the input noise to the output token sequence.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance with original unsupervised counterfactual learning and randomized topology methods; analysis of perturbation type and strength impact on performance.
COST: 19254
PREDICTION: The perturbed noising approach should allow the generator to effectively map the input noise to the output token sequence even in the presence of corruptions, leading to improved sampling quality and robustness.

PROPOSAL: To improve the effectiveness of the generator in learning a mapping from the input noise to the output token sequence, we will incorporate an adversarial training process into the one-step AR sampling method. Specifically, we will use a discriminator network to distinguish between the output token sequence produced by the generator and the actual output token sequence generated by the teacher AR model, and update the generator and discriminator parameters in parallel.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unsupervised One-Step AR Generator with Neural ODEs
PROPOSAL: We propose to leverage neural ordinary differential equations (ODEs) to train a one-step AR generator that matches the output distribution of a well-trained teacher AR model. Specifically, we will encode the teacher AR model's conditional probabilities as an ODE flow, such that the generator outputs a sequence of tokens by solving the ODE with a noise token as the initial condition.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed generator to DD1 and the teacher AR model itself, and also experiment with different ODE architectures and initial conditions.
COST: 10000 GHz
PREDICTION: Our method should outperform DD1 while being more efficient to train and less constrained by the predefined noise-to-data mapping, narrowing the quality gap to the original AR model. However, the ODE flow may be challenging to learn, leading to performance degradation or instability issues, particularly for larger images or more complex datasets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Graph Convolutional Network for Token Interaction Modeling
PROPOSAL: We propose to incorporate a graph convolutional network (GCN) into the one-step AR generator to model the complex interactions between tokens. Specifically, we will represent each token as a node in a graph, where edges between nodes encode the spatial relationships between tokens. The GCN will learn to transform the node features to capture the interaction patterns, and the generator will output the final token sequence based on the transformed node features.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed GCN-based generator to the generator with neural ODEs, and also experiment with different graph architectures and edge encodings.
COST: 13320 GHz
PREDICTION: The GCN-based generator should capture the local dependencies between tokens more effectively, leading to improved quality and efficiency. However, the GGCE be prone to overfitting or explicit over-smoothing, especially when the graph structure is complex or the sequence length is large.

TITLE: Multi-Resolution Hierarchical Attention for Tokenwise Distribution Modeling
PROPOSAL: We propose to incorporate a multi-resolution hierarchical attention mechanism into the one-step AR generator to model the tokenwise distributions. Specifically, we will use a hierarchical architecture with multiple attention heads and different receptive fields to capture the long-range and short-range relationships between tokens, and propagate the context information to different tokens with varying spatial granularities.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed generator to the generator with neural ODEs and GCN, and also experiment with different attention mechanisms and hierarchical structures.
COST: 18350 GHz
PREDICTION: The generator with multi-resolution hierarchical attention should capture the complex dependencies between tokens more effectively, leading to improved quality and efficiency. However, the generator may suffer from over- or under-extraction of features at different granularity levels, leading to performance degradation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learning to Debias the Teacher AR Model
PROPOSAL: We propose to learn a debiasing module that corrects the biases introduced by the teacher AR model, such that the one-step generator can produce more accurate and diverse outputs. Specifically, we will use a small neural network to predict the debiasing adjustments for each token, and apply these adjustments to the teacher AR model's output distribution.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed debiasing module to the revised generator with feedback connections, and also experiment with different debiasing architectures and adjustment methods.
COST: 20000 GHz
PREDICTION: The debiasing module should improve the quality and diversity of the generated token sequence, particularly in cases where the teacher AR model's biases lead to inaccurate or repetitive outputs. However, the debiasing module may introduce additional complexity and instability to the generator, especially if the debiasing adjustments are too aggressive.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Semi-Supervised Training of the One-Step Generator
PROPOSAL: We propose to develop a semi-supervised training framework that utilizes both unlabeled and labeled data to train the one-step generator. Specifically, we will use a small set of human-annotated data to supervise the generator's early stages, while using a large set of unlabeled data to fine-tune the generator and learn its distribution of outputs.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed semi-supervised training framework to fully supervised and unsupervised training methods, and also experiment with different labeling strategies and unlabeled data distribution.
COST: 75000 GHz
PREDICTION: The semi-supervised training framework should improve the quality and efficiency of the generator's training, particularly in cases where labeled data is scarce or expensive to obtain. However, the framework may require additional hyperparameter tuning and careful selection of the supervisory signal to ensure stable and convergent training.

TITLE: Pruning and Quantization of the One-Step Generator
PROPOSAL: We propose to develop pruning and quantization methods to reduce the number of parameters and bits required to represent the one-step generator, while preserving its accuracy and efficiency. Specifically, we will develop a hierarchical pruning strategy that targets the generator's modules, and apply quantization techniques to reduce the precision of weights and activations.

PREDICTION: The pruning and quantization methods should reduce the generator's computational complexity and memory requirements, particularly in resource-constrained environments or edge devices. However, the methods may lead to accuracy degradation, especially if the pruning or quantization is too aggressive.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Temporal Coherence Regularization for the One-Step Generator
PROPOSAL: We propose to develop a temporal coherence regularization (TCR) method that encourages the generator to produce outputs that are consistent with the temporal dependencies in the data. Specifically, we will use a variational Autoencoder (VAE) to model the temporal dependencies in the data, and use the resulting latent representation to guide the generator's output.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed TCR method to the generator without TCR, and also experiment with different VAE architectures and regularization strengths.
COST: 27000 GHz
PREDICTION: The TCR method should improve the quality and coherence of the generated token sequences, particularly in cases where the generator's outputs are not aligned with the underlying temporal structure of the data. However, the method may lead to overfitting or underfitting, especially if the TCR strength or VAE capacity are not carefully tuned.

PROPOSAL: We revise the pruning and quantization method to incorporate a transfer learning component that enables the pruned or quantized generator to leverage pre-trained knowledge from the original generator. Specifically, we will use a fine-tuning strategy to adapt the pruned or quantized generator to the specific task or dataset, while retaining some of the pre-trained knowledge from the original generator.
CONTROLS: We will compare the revised pruning and quantization method to the original method, and also experiment with different transfer learning strategies and adaptation rates.
COST: 55000 GHz
PREDICTION: The revised pruning and quantization method should improve the accuracy and efficiency of the pruned or quantized generator, particularly in cases where the pre-trained knowledge from the original generator is relevant to the task or dataset. However, the method may introduce additional computational overhead or requiring careful adjustment of hyperparameters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Structured Routing Loss for Expert Specialization
PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel routing loss component that is minimized when experts cover complementary subspaces of the input data. This structured loss encourages experts to specialize by promoting orthogonality of their learned representations. We propose to add this loss to the load-balancing loss, with a hyperparameter controlling the tradeoff between these competing objectives. The structured loss is computed as the sum of cosine similarities between the output representations of each pair of experts. We will explore different values of this hyperparameter on the benchmark dataset, and compare the effects on expert specialization and overall model performance.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposal against the baseline load-balancing loss and against the modified version of it that computes the loss over the whole batch.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: We expect to observe improved expert specialization and higher model performance on language modeling tasks, potentially while incurring some minor performance penalty if the tradeoff between the loss components is too strong. If not tuned carefully, the structured loss might exert too strong an influence on the expert weights, causing instability or catastrophic forgetting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Domain-Constrained Routing Loss
PROPOSAL: Generalize the structured routing loss from previous proposal to the multiple-domain setting, where experts are incentivized to specialize in specific domains. We propose a domain-constrained routing loss component that is minimized when experts for each domain cover complementary subspaces of the input data. This loss encourages experts to adapt to diverse domains more effectively and prevent domain neglect, i.e., inattention to some domains. We integrate this loss into the existing structured routing loss framework and explore its effects on expert specialization and model performance across a variety of domains, including English and Chinese language modeling.
CONTROLS: We will analyze the performance of non-domain-aware and domain-specific routing loss variants and compare them against the proposed domain-constrained routing loss.
COST: 6000
PREDICTION: We anticipate that incorporating domain knowledge into the routing loss will yield better expert specialization in each domain, including in English and Chinese language modeling, as well as enhanced model performance on tasks requiring expertise in multiple domains. However, the approach might add significant weight and make the model more difficult to train, particularly if the domain assignments are too simplistic.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Meta-Routing Learning with Hypernetworks
PROPOSAL: Introduce a hypernetwork that learns to adapt the routing structure of the MoE model to different tasks and domains. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Structured Routing Loss for Expert Specialization
PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel routing loss component that is minimized when experts cover complementary subspaces of the input data. This structured loss encourages experts to specialize by promoting orthogonality of their learned representations. We propose to add this loss to the load-balancing loss, with a hyperparameter controlling the tradeoff between these competing objectives. The structured loss is computed as the sum of cosine similarities between the output representations of each pair of experts. We will explore different values of this hyperparameter on the benchmark dataset, and compare the effects on expert specialization and overall model performance.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposal against the baseline load-balancing loss and against the modified version of it that computes the loss over the whole batch.
COST: 9000
PREDICTION: We expect to observe improved expert specialization and higher model performance on language modeling tasks, potentially while incurring some minor performance penalty if the tradeoff between the loss components is too strong. If not tuned carefully, the structured loss might exert too strong an influence on the expert weights, causing instability or catastrophic forgetting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Domain-Constrained Routing Loss
PROPOSAL: Generalize the structured routing loss from previous proposal to the multiple-domain setting, where experts are incentivized to specialize in specific domains. We propose a domain-constrained routing loss component that is minimized when experts for each domain cover complementary subspaces of the input data. This loss encourages experts to adapt to diverse domains more effectively and prevent domain neglect, i.e., inattention to some domains. We integrate this loss into the existing structured routing loss framework and explore its effects on expert specialization and model performance across a variety of domains, including English and Chinese language modeling.
CONTROLS: We will analyze the performance of non-domain-aware and domain-specific routing loss variants and compare them against the proposed domain-constrained routing loss.
COST: 18000
PREDICTION: We anticipate that incorporating domain knowledge into the routing loss will yield better expert specialization in each domain, including in English and Chinese language modeling, as well as enhanced model performance on tasks requiring expertise in multiple domains. However, the approach might add significant weight and make the model more difficult to train, particularly if the domain assignments are too simplistic.

TITLE: 2. Domain-Constrained Routing Loss
PROPOSAL: Introduce a clustering module after the routing matrix to group experts into clusters based on their learned representations, where each cluster represents a specific domain. This allows the model to automatically identify and adapt to diverse domains without prior knowledge of domain assignments. By re-routing tokens based on the cluster assignments, the model can be ensured that each token is routed to an expert within the same domain, promoting more accurate and robust domain specialization.
CONTROLS: We will ablate the clustering module to validate its effectiveness and analyze the components' interaction by comparing different clustering algorithms (e.g., k-means, hierarchical clustering).
COST: 27000
PREDICTION: By incorporating the clustering module, we expect to see better performance on multiple-domain adaptation and finer grain control over domain specialization. However, evaluating clustering stability and suppressing noisy clusters during the specialization process will be challenging. Poor-quality clustering might lead to a secondary bottleneck, introducing additional computational overhead, or producing erratic behavior in the routing mechanism.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Routing Weight Matrix Orthogonality Regularization
PROPOSAL: We propose to investigate the effectiveness of regularizing the orthogonality of the router's weight matrix in MoE language models. Unlike prior work that simply encourages the orthogonality of the entire weight matrix, including the load balancing coefficients, we will design a penalty term that focuses only on the routing weights, penalizing the inner product of the routing weights vectors, which would render the routing-vectors orthogonal. This will encourage more diverse routing patterns and steer experts to learn different, less-overlapping distributions.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard MoE with uniform load balancing loss; Ablations: No regularization, and different orthogonality penalties for routing weights only, routing weights and load balancing coefficients simultaneously.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: We expect to see a significant improvement in expert specialization and reduction in expert homogenization compared to the standard MoE baseline. Although this regularization approach might surge compute time due to introducing more trainable parameters, we project enhanced language modeling capabilities in exchange for this added modularity, but only mildly improved performance on mathematical reasoning and exam-style question answering tasks.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Imitation Learning for MoE Expert Routing
PROPOSAL: Inspired by recent work on learning routing algorithms, we design an imitation learning method that trains an MoE router using a set of pre-labeled expert activations. The target expert activation distribution is learned using a specialized algorithm, such as entropy-maximization-based routing, and the MoE router is trained to mimic this target distribution through a distance metric like KL-divergence. This will allow experts to learn different, more diverse, and potentially more meaningful distributions from the given data.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard MoE with uniform load balancing loss; Ablations: No pre-labeled expert activation (randomly initialize the router), imitation learning with different distance metrics and different target expert activation distributions.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: We anticipate an enhancement of expert specialization, driven in part by the explicit, interpretable nature of the labelled expert activations, which could confuse the model in more nuanced tasks that involve less obvious expert roles. We project improved downstream task performance, particularly in more conceptual understanding and reasoning-heavy tasks, due to the flexibility and generality gained from these diversified expert distributions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Task-Specific Routing for Multi-Domain Learning
PROPOSAL: Task-Specific Routing (TSR) is a strategy that modulates the routing of experts based on the specific task or sub-task being performed. By leveraging task information and incorporating it into the routing process, TSR enables the experts to learn task-specific functionalities, assigns suitable experts to good sub-tasks, and induces a hierarchical expertise within MoE models. TSR uses an auxiliary task-specific predictor to generate task-specific routing vectors.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard MoE with uniform load balancing loss; Ablations: No task-specific predictor, integrating task-specific information into routing without a predictor.
COST: 936
PREDICTION: We propose that TSR will promote expert specialization, especially when applied to large multi-domain learning contexts, allowing each expert to concentrate on a smaller, more precise, and well-defined niche of the overall dataset. However, task-specific routing might cause over-specialization, risking compromised global performance.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Task-Specific Routing for Multi-Domain Learning (Improved) 
PROPOSAL: Building upon Task-Specific Routing (TSR), we refine the approach by incorporating a task-agnostic information bottleneck (IB) which evaluates the relevance of input tokens, helping the experts to discover task-independent aspects of input data. This is achieved by introducing an auxiliary bottleneck that aggregates information from the task-specific features, providing a specialized intermediate representation that helps the models learn task-agnostic patterns. By using both task-specific and task-agnostic information, the experts gain additional guidance to facilitate knowledge sharing and the specialization of tasks.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard MoE with uniform load balancing loss; Previous TSR ablation; Introduced bottleneck ablation
COST: 1100
PREDICTION: We expect TSR with IB to enhance the global reasoning ability and exhibit better maintenance and relevance of domain knowledge for challenging multi-domain tasks, particularly with similar yet distinct sub-task domains. However, it might add a decrease in efficiency by introducing more learnable parameters, generating very parseable models that might experience diminished compression capabilities when operating under real-world constraits.

This attention mechanism encourages experts to specialize in specific subspaces of the input data and promotes expert collaboration.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard MoE with uniform load balancing loss; Ablations: Without attention, and using different attention loss functions.
COST: 36000
PREDICTION: By leveraging expert expertise to focus on specific regions of the input data, we anticipate improved downstream task performance, particularly in tasks that require domain-specific knowledge. The attention mechanism should also aid in reducing redundant expertise and enhancing expert collaboration, contributing to more robust and efficient model behavior.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Routing Weight Matrix Orthogonality Regularization
PROPOSAL: We propose to investigate the effectiveness of regularizing the orthogonality of the router's weight matrix in MoE language models. Unlike prior work that simply encourages the orthogonality of the entire weight matrix, including the load balancing coefficients, we will design a penalty term that focuses only on the routing weights, penalizing the inner product of the routing weights vectors, which would render the routing-vectors orthogonal. This will encourage more diverse routing patterns and steer experts to learn different, less-overlapping distributions.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard MoE with uniform load balancing loss; Ablations: No regularization, and different orthogonality penalties for routing weights only, routing weights and load balancing coefficients simultaneously.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: We expect to see a significant improvement in expert specialization and reduction in expert homogenization compared to the standard MoE baseline. Although this regularization approach might surge compute time due to introducing more trainable parameters, we project enhanced language modeling capabilities in exchange for this added modularity, but only mildly improved performance on mathematical reasoning and exam-style question answering tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Imitation Learning for MoE Expert Routing
PROPOSAL: Inspired by recent work on learning routing algorithms, we design an imitation learning method that trains an MoE router using a set of pre-labeled expert activations. The target expert activation distribution is learned using a specialized algorithm, such as entropy-maximization-based routing, and the MoE router is trained to mimic this target distribution through a distance metric like KL-divergence. This will allow experts to learn different, more diverse, and potentially more meaningful distributions from the given data.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard MoE with uniform load balancing loss; Ablations: No pre-labeled expert activation (randomly initialize the router), imitation learning with different distance metrics and different target expert activation distributions.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: We anticipate an enhancement of expert specialization, driven in part by the explicit, interpretable nature of the labelled expert activations, which could confuse the model in more nuanced tasks that involve less obvious expert roles. We project improved downstream task performance, particularly in more conceptual understanding and reasoning-heavy tasks, due to the flexibility and generality gained from these diversified expert distributions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Task-Specific Routing for Multi-Domain Learning
PROPOSAL: Task-Specific Routing (TSR) is a strategy that modulates the routing of experts based on the specific task or sub-task being performed. By leveraging task information and incorporating it into the routing process, TSR enables the experts to learn task-specific functionalities, assigns suitable experts to good sub-tasks, and induces a hierarchical expertise within MoE models. TSR uses an auxiliary task-specific predictor to generate task-specific routing vectors.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard MoE with uniform load balancing loss; Ablations: No task-specific predictor, integrating task-specific information into routing without a predictor.
COST: 2800
PREDICTION: We propose that TSR will promote expert specialization, especially when applied to large multi-domain learning contexts, allowing each expert to concentrate on a smaller, more precise, and well-defined niche of the overall dataset. However, task-specific routing might cause over-specialization, risking compromised global performance.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Task-Specific Routing for Multi-Domain Learning (Improved) 
PROPOSAL: Building upon Task-Specific Routing (TSR), we refine the approach by incorporating a task-agnostic information bottleneck (IB) which evaluates the relevance of input tokens, helping the experts to discover task-independent aspects of input data. This is achieved by introducing an auxiliary bottleneck that aggregates information from the task-specific features, providing a specialized intermediate representation that helps the models learn task-agnostic patterns. By using both task-specific and task-agnostic information, the experts gain additional guidance to facilitate knowledge sharing and the specialization of tasks.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard MoE with uniform load balancing loss; Previous TSR ablation; Introduced bottleneck ablation
COST: 3300
PREDICTION: We expect TSR with IB to enhance the global reasoning ability and exhibit better maintenance and relevance of domain knowledge for challenging multi-domain tasks, particularly with similar yet distinct sub-task domains. However, it might add a decrease in efficiency by introducing more learnable parameters, generating very parseable models that might experience diminished compression capabilities when operating under real-world constraits.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Orthogonal Routing Regularization for MoE Language Models
PROPOSAL: Explore the effect of adding a regularization term to the load-balancing loss that encourages the router's weight matrix to be orthogonal. This could be achieved by adding a term to the loss function:  lambda*||WW^T - I||^2, where W is the matrix of routing weights, I is the identity matrix, and lambda is a hyperparameter. We hypothesize that this regularization term would guide the experts towards specializing in different subspaces, thereby reducing expert homogenization.
CONTROLS: A baseline model trained with the standard load-balancing loss, as well as an ablation study on the effect of the regularization strength (how sensitive is the model's performance to the regularization term).
COST: 14400
PREDICTION: We expect this regularization term to improve the diversity of expert specialization, but it might not generalize to downstream tasks due to the absence of an explicit objective that aligns with the tasks. The effect might be more pronounced in models with a larger number of experts.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Structured Routing Diversity with Expert-Guided Adapters
PROPOSAL: We introduce two novel adapter components to the standard MoE architecture: routing diversity adapters and expert-language adapters. The routing diversity adapters are learnable sparse matrices that map the input embeddings to a space with structured routing diversity, essentially imposing constraints on which experts are used for specific tokens and contexts. Meanwhile, the expert-language adapters are affine transformations that enable each expert to specialize in processing specific linguistic structures, which are pre-defined as entities (entities, relationships, attributes), events, or sentiment. By adding these adapters to the standard MoE framework, the training objective can be designed to prioritize the growth of expert representation of these structures and structures-specific routing rules. This novel architecture, MoE-STAR (Structured routing Through Adapters and Routing), will be compared against unmodified MoE models on several tasks.
CONTROLS: MoE with routing within content planes (ROW) and MoE with shared stack as per indicative prior
COST: 108.9
PREDICTION: We expect MoE-STAR to outperform both baselines in downstream performance on knowledge-based tasks, including language modeling on large corpuses.trained for some periods the structure moderation balance might not be stable and needs to be proper trained and validated.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Multi-Label Image Classification via Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS)
PROPOSAL: Implement a meta-learning approach based on MCTS to dynamically adjust the training configuration of a multi-label image classifier (augmentation, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, and loss function) at each epoch, based on the model's current performance and training data characteristics. Use a given dataset and its corresponding validation set to optimize the MCTS hyperparameters.
CONTROLS: Compare against (1) static configuration (a baseline with the same model but fixed training configuration), (2) separate and offline optimization of individual configuration components via grid search, and (3) coreset-based MCTS that reduces the search space.
COST: 10,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach could yield significantly improved performance (at least +2% in mAP) compared to static configuration, and outperform separate optimization of configuration components, while reducing the risk of getting stuck in suboptimal configurations. Convergence and computational efficiency remain to be improved.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Training Configuration Selection (ATCS) for Multi-label Image Classification
PROPOSAL: We propose to develop a model-agnostic online optimization framework, ATCS, for dynamically selecting the training configuration across four core components: data augmentation, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, and loss function. ATCS will utilize a probabilistic model to learn the distribution over configurations at each training iteration, taking into account the evolving data characteristics and learning stages. By efficiently searching the configuration space online and adapting to changing conditions, ATCS will improve the model's ability to handle rare labels, stabilize training, and reduce convergence time.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: fixed static configuration; Baseline 2: separate, static adaptation of each component individually; Baseline 3: state-of-the-art automated machine learning.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: Expected to outperform static configurations and improve adaptability to rare labels, but may struggle with computational efficiency, potentially hindering its application to large datasets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Training Configuration Selection (ATCS) for Multi-label Image Classification
PROPOSAL: We propose to develop a model-agnostic online optimization framework, ATCS, for dynamically selecting the training configuration across four core components: data augmentation, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, and loss function. ATCS will utilize a probabilistic model to learn the distribution over configurations at each training iteration, taking into account the evolving data characteristics and learning stages. By efficiently searching the configuration space online and adapting to changing conditions, ATCS will improve the model's ability to handle rare labels, stabilize training, and reduce convergence time.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: fixed static configuration; Baseline 2: separate, static adaptation of each component individually; Baseline 3: state-of-the-art automated machine learning.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: Expected to outperform static configurations and improve adaptability to rare labels, but may struggle with computational efficiency, potentially hindering its application to large datasets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Augmentation-Optimizer Matching using Hybrid Gaussian Processes (AOM-HGP)
PROPOSAL: We propose to explore the use of hybrid Gaussian processes to model the joint distribution between data augmentation policies and optimizers. This will enable the identification of matching patterns and relationships between these components, which can be leveraged for online, adaptive selection. AOM-HGP will employ a sparse approximation of the process to reduce computational complexity, allowing for efficient training and usage over the course of the optimization process.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: random data augmentation policies; Baseline 2: fixed, mismatched optimizers; Baseline 3: state-of-the-art adaptive optimizers without cross-validation of augmentation policies.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: Expected to show improved adaptability and convergence rates, especially when employing optimal matching policies, but may struggle with convergence in the face of large search spaces.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REVISED Adaptive Loss Function Selection (ALFS) for class imbalance
PROPOSAL: We revise our initial proposal for Adaptive Loss Function Selection (ALFS). ALFS will not focus only on loss functions selection, but simultaneously co-select optimal learning rate schedules and augmentation policies that complement the chosen loss functions. By exploiting the inherent correspondence between the chosen loss function and evaluation metric, ALFS will rank loss functions and coordinate augmentations and learning rates accordingly, while adapting to the current training state and avoiding catastrophic interference.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: fixed loss function with static augmentation and learning rate; Baseline 2: re-weighted loss functions with separate, static adaptation of augmentation and learning rate; Baseline 3: re-weighted loss functions with adaptive optimizers.
COST: 4500
PREDICTION: Expected to achieve significant improvements in class-balanced performance, leveraging advanced co-selection strategies and principled adaptation to changing training conditions, and will potentially demonstrate superior results when tested on diverse datasets with class imbalance.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REVISED Adaptive Training Configuration Selection (ATCS) for Multi-label Image Classification
PROPOSAL: We revise our initial ATCS proposal to incorporate an additional mechanism to identify critical learning phases during training, where configurations that were previously satisfactory become suboptimal. By recognizing these phases, ATCS will dynamically adapt its configuration selection process to better respond to evolving training conditions, thus avoiding the limitations of fixed, static configurations.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: original static configuration; Baseline 2: revised ATCS with phase recognition mechanism off; Baseline 3: separate, static adaptation of each component individually.
COST: 3750
PREDICTION: Expected to provide more robust adaptability, coping with changes in critical learning phases, but may require additional computational resources for the enhanced phase-detection mechanism.

PROPOSAL: We propose a novel on-line dimensionality reduction technique tailored to the context of multi-label image classification. CONTROLS: Baseline 1: random search in high-dimensional configuration space; Baseline 2: fixed, offline dimensionality reduction; Baseline 3: standard grid search with distinct static configurations.
COST: 5400
PREDICTION: Expected to significantly accelerate the adaptation process, lead to improved robustness, but the selection of meaningful embeddings is hard; poorly tuned embeddings must be thoroughly tested against training dataset.

TITLE: Hybrid Meta-Learning for Adaptive Multi-Label Image Classification
PROPOSAL: We propose a meta-learning approach that combines the strengths of model-based and model-free meta-learning methods to adaptively adjust the training components (data augmentation, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, and loss function) over the course of training. This hybrid approach will utilize a model-based method (such as neural reaching) to adapt the data augmentation, and a model-free method (such as gradient matching) to adapt the optimizer and the learning-rate schedule. The loss function will be adapted based on the trained model's performance on the validation set.
CONTROLS: We will compare our method with a random search of the configuration space, and several state-of-the-art adaptive methods for individual components (such as trained augmentation policies, adaptive optimizers, cyclical learning-rate schedules).
COST: 432.13 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our hybrid meta-learning method should outperform the state-of-the-art adaptive methods for individual components, and achieve higher final performance and better handling of rare labels than a static configuration. However, the method may suffer from higher training time and computational resources required for meta-learning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dynamically Weighted Joint Optimization of Training Components
PROPOSAL: We propose an online joint optimization method that adaptively adjusts the importance of each training component (data augmentation, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, and loss function) during training. This is achieved by dynamically weighting the loss functions for each component based on their individual performance and interaction with the model. We will employ a gradient-based method to update the weights, ensuring that the optimal configuration is reached gradually throughout training.
CONTROLS: We will compare our method with the Hybrid Meta-Learning approach (Proposal 1), as well as several state-of-the-art joint optimization methods (such as automated machine learning and neural architecture search) with reduced computational costs (e.g., modified to focus on a smaller subset of components).
COST: 670 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our dynamically weighted joint optimization method should yield better control over the trade-off between individual component performance and overall model performance, compared to the Hybrid Meta-Learning approach. This may result in improved convergence and classification accuracy for rare labels. However, optimal weight initialization and learning rate setting may require careful tuning.

TITLE: Adversarial-Based Inter-Component Coordination for Multi-Label Image Classification
PROPOSAL: We propose an adversarial-based approach to coordinate the interactions among the training components (data augmentation, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, and loss function). Specifically, we will employ a generator-discriminator framework to simulate competition among components and encourage their cooperation. The generator will attempt to modify the training components to maximize performance, while the discriminator evaluates and penalizes attempts that degrade performance.
CONTROLS: We will compare our approach with the state-of-the-art adaptive methods (such as learned augmentation policies and adaptive optimizers) and the Dynamically Weighted Joint Optimization method (Proposal 2).
COST: 1018.8 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our adversarial-based inter-component coordination approach should improve the overall performance and stability of the model by promoting cooperation among the training components. However, the optimal architecture of the generator and discriminator may require careful tuning, and may suffer from exploration-exploitation trade-offs in the coordination process.

TITLE: Hierarchical Training Component Optimization (HTCO)
PROPOSAL: Introduce a hierarchical optimization framework for training components that incorporates both local and global optimization techniques. The first stage uses a MOO (Multi-Objective Optimization) strategy to find the optimal set of hyperparameters for each component, treating each component as a separate optimization problem. In the second stage, the configuration is further refined using a CMA-ES (Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy) algorithm, which explores the trade-offs between competing objectives. This two-stage optimization process allows HTCO to efficiently search for configurations that balance competing objectives and minimize the impact of local optima.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of HTCO to that of OJO and ACO on real-world multi-label datasets with class imbalance, as well as to other state-of-the-art methods.

PREDICTION: HTCO should demonstrate robust performance on real-world datasets with class imbalance, as it leverages the strengths of both local and global optimization techniques to find optimal configurations. However, the computational cost of HTCO's two-stage optimization process may be higher than that of ACO or OJO.

TITLE: Investigating Model Performance Deterioration due to Activation Quantization
PROPOSAL: 
We will revisit our baseline billion-scale model, the Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer (VGGT), and carefully quantify the impact of various activation quantization strategies on its performance in a multi-view 3D reconstruction task.
We will use the prevalent datasets in this field, specifically KITTI for camera pose estimation, ScanNet and SURE4D for point map and point cloud reconstruction, to compare against the full-precision baseline. In particular, we utilize metrics like ADE-3D, NIQE, and point cloud accuracy, to assess the strengths and weaknesses of different quantization methods and target bits, surveying a range of MPNIST, INT8, and INT4 quantization schemes. To handle the extreme variance caused by the data-independent special tokens, we experiment with clipping budgets to prevent outliers, reweighting loss functions, and enforcing a min-max normalization over activations for bits as low as INT4. ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Special Token-aware Calibration Strategies for Efficient and Robust Post-Training Quantization
PROPOSAL: 
In this proposal, we focus on developing a novel approach to efficiently and robustly calibrate the weights and activations of VGGT, with a particular emphasis on addressing the challenges posed by data-independent special tokens. We draw inspiration from the special token-aware taxonomy proposed in Task 2, and introduce a range of new calibration techniques tailored to each of the categories therein. Specifically, we propose to: (a) employ a probabilistic sequence model to learn a robust distribution over the special token embeddings; (b) employ a generalized mean-std adaptation scheme to handle the high variance caused by the special tokens; and (c) utilize a multi-objective optimization strategy to jointly learn the quantization scaling factors and learnable token embeddings, while ensuring that the model's performance on downstream tasks remains resilient to quantization errors. We evaluate these strategies on a set of representative tasks within the multi-view 3D reconstruction domain, and anticipate that our special token-aware calibration approach will enable efficient and robust deployment of billion-scale models like VGGT in resource-constrained settings.
CONTROLS: As part of this task, we will carry out extensive ablation studies on the three proposed calibration strategies, comparing their performance against a range of strong baselines and exploring their interactions with different quantization techniques and special token configurations.
COST: 18350
PREDICTION: By leveraging the insights from our special token-aware taxonomy and the robust calibration strategies proposed herein, we expect to achieve a significant reduction in the computational resources required to deploy VGGT, while ensuring that its performance on downstream tasks remains comparable to that of the full-precision model.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Robust Regularization for Special Token-based 3D Reconstruction Transformers
PROPOSAL: 
This proposal focuses on introducing a novel regularization framework for special token-based 3D reconstruction transformers like VGGT, designed to promote more robust and generalizable representation learning in the face of extreme activation variance associated with data-independent special tokens. Our approach consists of three key components: (a) a token-level dropout scheme to reduce over-reliance on special tokens; (b) a learned similarity-based penalty term to discourage special token embeddings from dominating the activation distribution; and (c) a gradient-based annealing framework to encourage more uniform exploration of the model's expressiveness. We empirically evaluate our proposed regularizers on a range of challenging 3D reconstruction tasks, demonstrating that they can improve the robustness and generalizability of special token-based models, while providing a more nuanced understanding of the interplay between special token regularization and model quantization.
CONTROLS: We will perform an ablation analysis on the different regularization components, and compare the performance of our approach against a range of strong baselines, including traditional weight decay and early stopping.
COST: 20000
PREDICTION: By leveraging the insights from our regularization framework, we anticipate that we can improve the robustness and generalizability of special token-based models, enabling more accurate 3D reconstruction and camera pose estimation in challenging and unseen scenarios.

TITLE: Evaluating the Transferability of Post-Training Quantization Across 3D Reconstruction Tasks and Datasets
PROPOSAL: 
In this proposal, we seek to systematically evaluate the transferability of post-training quantization (PTQ) across different 3D reconstruction tasks and datasets. We will leverage our previously proposed taxonomy and calibration strategies to conduct a thorough analysis of PTQ's adaptability, exploring how well it can be transferred from one task to another, and whether its performance is sensitive to dataset-specific characteristics. Our evaluation will focus on a range of tasks, including camera pose estimation, point map regression, and point cloud reconstruction, and will involve extensive experimentation on various datasets, including KITTI, ScanNet, and SURE4D. We anticipate that our investigation will provide valuable insights into PTQ's transferability and shed light on the key factors that influence its adaptability across different 3D reconstruction tasks and datasets.
CONTROLS: As part of this task, we will perform a comprehensive ablation study on the hyperparameters and configurations used in our PTQ evaluation, as well as examine the impact of different source tasks and datasets on PTQ's transferability.
COST: 23328
PREDICTION: By systematically evaluating the transferability of PTQ across different 3D reconstruction tasks and datasets, we anticipate that we can identify the key factors that influence PTQ's adaptability and provide valuable insights for its application in real-world 3D reconstruction scenarios.

PROPOSAL:

We will investigate how to combine the benefits of PTQ, which includes reduced model size and improved inference speed, with the knowledge distillation approach, which enables more efficient model training and better generalization. Our approach will involve designing a novel distillation framework that leverages PTQ to efficiently distill knowledge from a large teacher model to a smaller student model, while preserving the robustness and accuracy of the distilled model. We anticipate that our approach will provide a more efficient and robust solution for 3D reconstruction modeling, with potential applications in real-world scenarios.

COST: 33386.23
PREDICTION: By integrating post-training quantization and knowledge distillation, we anticipate that we can develop a more efficient and robust 3D reconstruction model, with improved inference speed and better generalization, while maintaining its accuracy and robustness.

TITLE: Post-Training Quantization of 3D Reconstruction Transformers via Data Augmentation
PROPOSAL: We will explore the potential of data augmentation for improving post-training quantization of VGGT on multi-view 3D reconstruction tasks. Specifically, we will randomly jitter input frames, apply random camera pose perturbations, or simulate image noise, to increase the diversity of the calibration set. Our hypothesis is that by amplifying the complexity and variability of the input data, we can capture a more representative portion of the activation distributions and improve quantization accuracy on unseen scenes.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: REVISED Diverse Calibration Sets for VGGT Quantization
PROPOSAL: 
Instead of simply combining frames from various objects, indoor scenes, and disjoint views, we propose to create multiple calibration sets by sampling diverse scenes from real-world benchmark datasets, such as the NYU Depth V2 and Scannet datasets, with a focus on scenarios that are hardest to generalize, including:

* Diverse lighting conditions (e.g., day, night, dimly lit, etc.)
* Varied viewpoints (e.g., frontal, side, top-down, etc.)
* Different object scales (e.g., small objects, large objects, etc.)
* Object in motion
* Scenes with multiple objects and complex geometries

To prepare these calibration sets, we will apply a model-based data augmentation pipeline using a low-cost 3D reconstruction model (e.g., COLMAP) to create synthetic data for each scene. This will increase the sample size and data diversity while maintaining a computationally efficient process.

Controls: baseline calibration datasets (e.g., random sampling from NYU Depth V2)

COST: 10000
PREDICTION: The revised calibration sets will improve the robustness and accuracy of the quantization results, particularly in challenging scenarios, but may require careful tuning to avoid overfitting to the augmentation pipeline.

TITLE: REVISED Diverse Calibration Sets for VGGT Quantization
PROPOSAL: 
Instead of simply combining frames from various objects, indoor scenes, and disjoint views, we propose to create multiple calibration sets by sampling diverse scenes from real-world benchmark datasets, such as the NYU Depth V2 and Scannet datasets, with a focus on scenarios that are hardest to generalize, including:

* Diverse lighting conditions (e.g., day, night, dimly lit, etc.)
* Varied viewpoints (e.g., frontal, side, top-down, etc.)
* Different object scales (e.g., small objects, large objects, etc.)
* Object in motion
* Scenes with multiple objects and complex geometries

To prepare these calibration sets, we will apply a model-based data augmentation pipeline using a low-cost 3D reconstruction model (e.g., COLMAP) to create synthetic data for each scene. This will increase the sample size and data diversity while maintaining a computationally efficient process.

Controls: baseline calibration datasets (e.g., random sampling from NYU Depth V2)

COST: 90000
PREDICTION: The revised calibration sets will improve the robustness and accuracy of the quantization results, particularly in challenging scenarios, but may require careful tuning to avoid overfitting to the augmentation pipeline.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Knowledge Distillation for Efficient Quantization of VGGT
PROPOSAL: 
To leverage the strengths of the original VGGT model while accelerating its inference speed, we propose a knowledge distillation approach to quantize VGGT. Specifically, we will train a smaller student model (e.g., half the size of VGGT) to mimic the behavior of the original VGGT model on a calibration set. The student model will then be quantized using a readily available quantization framework (e.g., post-training quantization with histogram-based quantization).

To enable efficient knowledge distillation, we will incorporate a dual-temperature method to improve the student model's learning efficiency and robustness. Additionally, we will employ an entropy-based attention mechanism to focus the student model's learning on critical regions of the input data.

Controls: cold start training the student model from scratch, no attention mechanism, or directly quantizing the original VGGT model without knowledge distillation.

COST: 13320
PREDICTION: Knowledge distillation will significantly improve the accuracy and robustness of the quantized VGGT model, but may require careful tuning of the student model's size, temperature, and attention mechanism to avoid overfitting.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: GPU-Accelerated VGGT Pruning and Quantization
PROPOSAL: 
To further accelerate the inference speed of VGGT, we propose a complementary approach that combines pruning and quantization techniques. Specifically, we will prune the VGGT model using a combination of magnitude-based pruning and filter-based pruning to reduce the model's size and compute requirements.

Subsequently, we will apply a specialized quantization framework that leverages the pruned model's sparse structure to accelerate the quantization process. We will also investigate the benefits of parallelizing the pruning and quantization processes to take full advantage of modern GPU architectures.

Controls: pruning-only approach, quantization-only approach, or a combination of pruning and quantization without parallelization.

COST: 20000
PREDICTION: Pruning and quantization will accelerate the inference speed of VGGT by an additional factor of 2-3, but may require careful tuning of the pruning ratios and quantization parameters to maintain accuracy.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Multi-Task Training for Robust VGGT Quantization
PROPOSAL: 
To improve the robustness and generalization of VGGT quantization, we propose a multi-task training approach that trains the quantized VGGT model on multiple 3D tasks simultaneously (e.g., depth estimation, point cloud reconstruction, camera pose estimation). This will enable the model to learn a more robust and transferable representation that is less sensitive to specific task requirements.

To achieve this, we will employ a multi-task learning objective that combines the losses from each individual task, as well as a regularization term to promote representation sharing between tasks. We will also investigate the benefits of using task-specific heads and losses to improve performance.

Controls: single-task training, no regularization, or using a different multi-task learning objective.

COST: 23328
PREDICTION: Multi-task training will improve the robustness and generalization of VGGT quantization, but may require careful tuning of the task losses and regularization terms to avoid overfitting.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Evaluating the Transferability of VGGT Quantization Across Datasets
PROPOSAL: 
To investigate the transferability of VGGT quantization across different datasets, we propose a comprehensive evaluation framework that assesses the performance of quantized VGGT on a variety of 3D benchmarks (e.g., NYU Depth V2, Scannet, Matterport3D). This will help identify the robustness and generalizability of our proposed quantization methods.

We will evaluate the performance of quantized VGGT on each benchmark using a range of metrics (e.g., depth accuracy, point cloud accuracy, camera pose accuracy), and compare the results to those obtained with full-precision VGGT and other state-of-the-art methods.

Controls: evaluating only a subset of benchmarks, or using different evaluation metrics.

COST: 27000
PREDICTION: The evaluation framework will reveal the transferability and robustness of VGGT quantization across various benchmarks, but may also highlight potential challenges and limitations of the quantization methods.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: A Hybrid Quantization Framework for High-Accuracy and Efficient VGGT
PROPOSAL: 
To integrate the benefits of different quantization methods, we propose a hybrid quantization framework that combines the strengths of knowledge distillation, pruning, and adaptive quantization schemes. This framework will leverage the knowledge distillation method to learn a high-capacity student model, and then apply pruning and adaptive quantization schemes to achieve high accuracy and efficiency.

Specifically, we will first distill the VGGT model to obtain a high-capacity student model using a dual-temperature knowledge distillation framework. Then, we will apply pruning to reduce the model's size and accelerate computation. Finally, we will adopt adaptive quantization schemes to further improve accuracy and efficiency.

Controls: using only knowledge distillation, or using only pruning and adaptive quantization schemes.

COST: 40000
PREDICTION: The hybrid quantization framework will achieve state-of-the-art accuracy and efficiency for VGGT, but may require careful tuning of the model architecture and hyperparameters to optimize performance.

TITLE:  Investigating Effective Calibration for PTQ of VGGT
PROPOSAL: We will utilize various calibration methods such as iterative calibration, knowledge distillation, and entropy-based calibration to determine the optimal quantization ranges for the special tokens in VGGT. For this, we will leverage the Model Compression Benchmark, which provides a suite of metrics to evaluate model compression and acceleration, to ensure accurate and robust results. We will compare the performance of different calibration methods and analyze the trade-offs between computational complexity, calibration data size, and model quality.
CONTROLS: Compare with unconstrained quantization, standard PTQ, and knowledge distillation-based PTQ with fixed special tokens
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: Our proposed calibration methods will outperform standard PTQ on certain tasks due to their improved ability to capture complex activation distributions. However, the effectiveness of calibration methods may degrade on real-world data with limited calibration samples, leading to performance drops in certain scenes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Robust Quantization Design for Special Tokens
PROPOSAL: We will design a robust quantization scheme specifically tailored for the special tokens in VGGT. This will involve analyzing the critical features that contribute to the extreme variance seen in activation distributions and developing a dual-quantization strategy where we apply standard quantization to regular image tokens and dedicated quantization scheme to special tokens. Our goal is to minimize information loss without compromising model performance. We will evaluate the proposed method on various 3D reconstruction tasks.
CONTROLS: Baseline our dual-quantization method against the original VGGT, PTQ with standard quantization, and PTQ with separate quantization for special tokens
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Our dual-quantization strategy will significantly reduce performance drops caused by standard quantization on special tokens, especially in vision tasks with intricate geometric and texture details. It may lead to performance degradation on select datasets if the specially designed quantization does not capture task-specific information.

PROPOSAL: We will utilize various calibration methods such as iterative calibration, knowledge distillation, and entropy-based calibration to determine the optimal quantization ranges for the special tokens in VGGT. For this, we will leverage the Model Compression Benchmark, which provides a suite of metrics to evaluate model compression and acceleration, to ensure accurate and robust results. We will compare the performance of different calibration methods and analyze the trade-offs between computational complexity, calibration data size, and model quality.

COST: 3000

However, the effectiveness of calibration methods may degrade on real-world data with limited calibration samples, leading to performance drops in certain scenes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Robust Quantization Design for Special Tokens
PROPOSAL: We will design a robust quantization scheme specifically tailored for the special tokens in VGGT. This will involve analyzing the critical features that contribute to the extreme variance seen in activation distributions and developing a dual-quantization strategy where we apply standard quantization to regular image tokens and dedicated quantization scheme to special tokens. Our goal is to minimize information loss without compromising model performance. We will evaluate the proposed method on various 3D reconstruction tasks.
CONTROLS: Baseline our dual-quantization method against the original VGGT, PTQ with standard quantization, and PTQ with separate quantization for special tokens

PREDICTION: Our dual-quantization strategy will significantly reduce performance drops caused by standard quantization on special tokens, especially in vision tasks with intricate geometric and texture details. ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Bootstrap PTQ with Adaptive Token Weighting
PROPOSAL: We propose to develop a PTQ framework that adaptively weights the learned special tokens and the regular image tokens based on the magnitude of their activations. This institutes temporal-channel-wise attention in quantization, which helps balance global channel information with local losses. Inspired by self-modulating networks, we add trainable scaling factors to both the special token embeddings and the regular token embeddings to dynamically adjust their contributions based on the dominant regions of the activation pattern. This ensures both key high-variable parts and redundant regions do not subserve loss in the quantization range, compelling quantization range fit. We employ pre-training PTQ losses, but differ from existing methods through actively developing samples with adjustment factor such as analyzing transition point in loss toward vary arrangement, which integrates variations in feature spatial chains so as enable significant bin range reduction while retaining pre-training model performance.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Bootstrap PTQ with Adaptive Token Weighting
PROPOSAL: We revise our initial adaptive token weighting proposal to introduce a more controlled approach to handling the special tokens' extreme variance. Specifically, we implement a learned "token pruning" mechanism, which allows the model to automatically identify and down-weight the most variance-prone special tokens during quantization. This approach is more data-efficient and requires fewer additional parameters compared to our initial bootstrap PTQ design. We also evaluate the impact of token importance on model performance, using a stratified sampling strategy to study the relationship between token weights, quantization accuracy, and validation performance.
CONTROLS: We compare against our initial bootstrap PTQ design, as well as a baseline PTQ approach that does not utilize token prunning.
COST: 1827

PREDICTION: Expect significant improvement in downstream performance metrics, such as point cloud reconstruction and camera pose estimation accuracy, as a result of the adaptive token weighting and pruning mechanisms.

TITLE: Meta-PTQ: A Multi-Task PTQ Framework for Efficient 3D Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: We propose a meta-PTQ framework that tackles the challenges of PTQ for 3D reconstruction by learning to adapt to multiple downstream tasks. Our framework, called Meta-PTQ, consists of a meta-model that is trained on a diverse set of 3D reconstruction tasks, including point cloud reconstruction, camera pose estimation, and depth estimation. During inference, the meta-model generates a task-specific PTQ configuration for each downstream task, allowing us to achieve state-of-the-art performance on a range of 3D reconstruction tasks with minimal additional computational overhead.
CONTROLS: We compare Meta-PTQ against a range of baselines, including single-task PTQ and ensemble methods, and demonstrate its superior performance on tasks such as ShapeNet and CHALET.
COST: 7833
PREDICTION: Expect significant improvements in downstream performance metrics, such as point cloud reconstruction error and camera pose estimation accuracy, due to the meta-model's ability to adapt to different downstream tasks.

TITLE: Meta-PTQ: A Multi-Task PTQ Framework for Efficient 3D Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: We revise our previous proposal for Meta-PTQ to incorporate a stronger prior for task-specific quantization, based on the observation that different 3D reconstruction tasks have distinct patterns of data-dependent special tokens. To this end, we introduce a task-conditioned token transformation layer, which learns to adapt the token embedding space for each downstream task based on its specific characteristics. This enables Meta-PTQ to better capture task-specific patterns in the PTQ configuration, leading to improved performance on a range of 3D reconstruction tasks.
CONTROLS: We compare against our initial meta-PTQ proposal, as well as a range of ablations and baselines, including single-task PTQ and KL-weighted task-conditioning.
COST: 3300

PREDICTION: Expect improved performance on downstream tasks, particularly those with distinct patterns of data-dependent special tokens, such as point cloud reconstruction and camera pose estimation.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: On the Interplay Between PTQ and Special Token Embeddings
PROPOSAL: We investigate the interplay between post-training quantization (PTQ) and special token embeddings in multi-view 3D reconstruction transformers. Our analysis reveals that PTQ can induce significant changes in the special token embedding space, particularly for data-independent special tokens. We propose a novel two-stage PTQ algorithm that takes into account the learned special token embeddings during quantization, leading to improved performance on 3D reconstruction tasks. Our approach, called PTQ-Special, learns a special token embedding adapter that refines the quantization configuration based on the learned token embeddings.
CONTROLS: We compare against our previous proposals, as well as a range of ablations and baselines, including single-task PTQ and PTQ with random special token embeddings.
COST: 4737.79
PREDICTION: Expect improved performance on downstream tasks, particularly those that rely heavily on special token embeddings, such as camera pose estimation and point cloud reconstruction.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Exploring Domain-Adversarial Calibration for VGGT
PROPOSAL: We revise our previous proposal to incorporate a more efficient and scalable approach to domain-adversarial calibration. Specifically, we propose to use a contrastive learning framework to calibrate the VGGT model across multiple domains, allowing for more efficient and robust calibration. Our approach, called CAL-PTQ, learns to distinguish between calibrated and non-calibrated examples, and adapts the quantization configuration based on the contrastive loss. This enables CAL-PTQ to achieve state-of-the-art performance on 3D reconstruction tasks while reducing the computational overhead of domain-adversarial calibration.
CONTROLS: We compare against our previous proposals, as well as a range of ablations and baselines, including single-task PTQ and PTQ with random calibration.
COST: 5200

PREDICTION: Expect improved performance on downstream tasks, particularly those that benefit from domain-adversarial calibration, such as camera pose estimation and point cloud reconstruction, while reducing the computational overhead.

TITLE: VGGT-Sparse: A Sparsity-Inspired PTQ Framework for Efficient 3D Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: We propose a new PTQ framework, called VGGT-Sparse, that leverages sparsity-inspired techniques to efficiently reduce the computational overhead of 3D reconstruction transformers like VGGT. Our framework adopts a novel sparse-attention mechanism that selectively prunes attention weights based on their contribution to the model's output. This leads to significant reductions in both computational and memory requirements, while maintaining high accuracy on 3D reconstruction tasks.
CONTROLS: We compare against our previous proposals, as well as a range of ablations and baselines, including single-task PTQ and PTQ with random pruning.

TITLE: Bi-Modal Decision Transformer for Continuous Control
PROPOSAL: 
Train a DPT-based model that employs a bi-modal action distribution to better capture complex continuous action posteriors. The bi-modal distribution will be comprised of two component distributions: a centered, spherical normal distribution modeling confident actions from the posterior, and a beta-negative binomial distribution for uncertain, exploratory actions.
CONTROLS: 
- Baselines: Vanilla DPT, Transformer-based algorithms like MazeRL and Meta-RL
- Ablations: Experiments with single-modal action distributions and without the beta-negative binomial component
- Controls: Computation of metrics and normalizers with respect to each sub-component and the full bi-modal action distribution
COST: 2700
PREDICTION: 
The bi-modal model is expected to exhibit improved performance on unseen tasks and domain variations, particularly in high-dimensional action spaces. However, ablations may reveal that the centered normal distribution is not crucial for performance gains.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Action Representation Learning for Scalable In-Context Learning
PROPOSAL: 
Propose a hierarchical action representation learning framework to leverage offline data for multi-modal continuous action posteriors. This framework will learn an initial low-dimensional embedding of actions using a contrastive loss, followed by a higher-level transformer network that refines this representation and generates the final action distribution. This hierarchical structure allows the model to learn nuanced action relationships and distill complex behavior from offline data.
CONTROLS: 
- Baselines: Vanilla DPT, Multi-Layer Perceptron-(MLP)-based action representation models
- Ablations: Experiments without the initial contrastive loss, with a fixed, low-dimensional embedding, and comparing the hierarchical structure against a single-level model
- Controls: Computation of metrics and normalizers with respect to each sub-component and the full hierarchical model
COST: 4,000
PREDICTION: 
This hierarchical representation learning framework is expected to significantly improve in-context learning capabilities for continuous control tasks with diverse action spaces. However, training this model may be more computationally intensive, and ablation results could highlight the importance of the initial contrastive loss for learning compact action embeddings.

Introduce a dynamic context modulation mechanism to adapt the in-context learning process between tasks with different MDP structures and requirements. By incorporating task-agnostic, flexible network modules that adaptively adjust to the current task and context, the model will learn to selectively incorporate task-external knowledge, distilling expertise from diverse domains and domains of expertise for effective transfer.
CONTROLS: 
- Baselines: Vanilla DPT, static context aggregators, and context-invariant architectures
- Ablations: Experiments with different module designs, different learning and transfer objectives
- Controls: Computation of metrics and normalizers with respect to each sub-component and the full dynamic context model
COST: 4,665.6
PREDICTION: 
This dynamic context modulation approach is expected to significantly improve transfer and domain generalization for the DPT, allowing it to effectively leverage diverse domain expertise and seamlessly adapt to new unseen tasks and environments. However, the adaptability of the modules and the choice of learning objectives will require careful tuning to ensure interpretable context modulation and balanced exploration.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Exploration via Reward Augmentation in Decision Transformers
PROPOSAL: 
Introduce a reward augmentation mechanism to the Decision Transformer, allowing the model to efficiently explore new environments and adapt to novel reward structures without requiring additional task-specific training. By augmenting the standard reward signal with learned fitness functions, the model will guide itself towards exploring uncharted regions of the state-action space during in-context learning.
CONTROLS: 
- Baselines: Vanilla DPT, MAML and Prophet with manually crafted exploration objectives
- Ablations: Experiments with different baseline predictors and augmentation techniques
- Controls: Computation of metrics and normalizers with respect to each sub-component and the full reward augmentation model
COST: 6,700
PREDICTION: 
This reward augmentation mechanism is expected to significantly enhance the DPT's exploration capabilities, enabling it to rapidly discover novel actions and adapt to diverse reward structures without being overly reliant on task-specific in-context learning. However, carefully designing the baseline predictors and augmentation techniques will be necessary to ensure the reward augmentation aligns with the model's incentive structures without promoting unnecessary exploration or convergence issues.

TITLE: Posterior Regularization for Improving DPT Interpretability
PROPOSAL: 
Develop a posterior regularization framework to improve the interpretability of the Decision Transformer by promoting posterior distributions that are closer to the assumed Bayesian posterior. This framework will use regularization terms to encourage the model's output posterior distribution to be centered around a specific prior distribution, leading to more interpretable and robust action recommendations.
CONTROLS: 
- Baselines: Vanilla DPT without regularization, learned posterior approximations
- Ablations: Experiments with different regularization terms, prior distributions, and hyperparameters
- Controls: Computation of metrics and normalizers with respect to each sub-component and the full regularization model
COST: 7,340
PREDICTION: 
This posterior regularization approach is expected to significantly improve the interpretability of the DPT, enabling more effective action selection and transferability in new tasks and environments. However, careful tuning of the regularization terms and prior distributions will be necessary to avoid over-smoothing or under-regularization of the posterior.

TITLE: Meta-Domain Adaptation for Large Action Models
PROPOSAL: 
Develop a meta-domain adaptation framework to enable the Decision Transformer to adapt to unseen tasks and domains at test time, using prior knowledge learned from a few related domains. This framework will learn to transfer generalizable action representations and policies across domains, further improving the model's ability to generalize and perform well on diverse, unseen tasks.
CONTROLS: 
- Baselines: Vanilla DPT, single-task adaptation, few-shot domain adaptation
- Ablations: Experiments with different meta-learning architectures, iterative adaptation procedures, and benchmark domains
- Controls: Computation of metrics and normalizers with respect to each sub-component and the full meta-domain adaptation model
COST: 8,295
PREDICTION: 
This meta-domain adaptation approach is expected to significantly enhance the Decision Transformer's ability to generalize and perform well on unseen tasks and domains, leveraging prior knowledge from related domains to facilitate efficient adaptation. However, designing effective meta-learning architectures and adaptation procedures will be crucial to ensure that the model can adapt to novel tasks and domains without compromising performance on the original set of domains.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Bi-Modal Decision Transformer for Continuous Control
PROPOSAL: 
Train a DPT-based model that employs a bi-modal action distribution to better capture complex continuous action posteriors. The bi-modal distribution will be comprised of two component distributions: a centered, spherical normal distribution modeling confident actions from the posterior, and a beta-negative binomial distribution for uncertain, exploratory actions.
CONTROLS: 
- Baselines: Vanilla DPT, Transformer-based algorithms like MazeRL and Meta-RL
- Ablations: Experiments with single-modal action distributions and without the beta-negative binomial component
- Controls: Computation of metrics and normalizers with respect to each sub-component and the full bi-modal action distribution
COST: 8000
PREDICTION: 
The bi-modal model is expected to exhibit improved performance on unseen tasks and domain variations, particularly in high-dimensional action spaces. However, ablations may reveal that the centered normal distribution is not crucial for performance gains.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Action Representation Learning for Scalable In-Context Learning
PROPOSAL: 
Propose a hierarchical action representation learning framework to leverage offline data for multi-modal continuous action posteriors. This framework will learn an initial low-dimensional embedding of actions using a contrastive loss, followed by a higher-level transformer network that refines this representation and generates the final action distribution. This hierarchical structure allows the model to learn nuanced action relationships and distill complex behavior from offline data.
CONTROLS: 
- Baselines: Vanilla DPT, Multi-Layer Perceptron-(MLP)-based action representation models
- Ablations: Experiments without the initial contrastive loss, with a fixed, low-dimensional embedding, and comparing the hierarchical structure against a single-level model
- Controls: Computation of metrics and normalizers with respect to each sub-component and the full hierarchical model
COST: 12,000
PREDICTION: 
This hierarchical representation learning framework is expected to significantly improve in-context learning capabilities for continuous control tasks with diverse action spaces. However, training this model may be more computationally intensive, and ablation results could highlight the importance of the initial contrastive loss for learning compact action embeddings.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REVISED Title: Improving Action Distribution Modeling for DPT
PROPOSAL: 
REVISION: 
Refine the bi-modal action distribution in the Bi-Modal Decision Transformer by replacing the beta-negative binomial component with a more expressive, adaptive probabilistic model, such as a mixture-of-normals distribution. This refined model will enable the DPT to better capture complex continuous action posteriors and adapt to varying task and domain characteristics.
CONTROLS: 
- Ablations: Experiments comparing the original bi-modal distribution to the revised mixture-of-normals model, individual component-wise improvements
- Baselines: Vanilla DPT
COST: 10,000
PREDICTION: 
This revised model is expected to outperform the original bi-modal distribution, offering improved performance on unseen tasks and domain variations. However, the revised distribution might be more computationally intensive to sample from and may not always preserve the interpretable posterior sampling behavior of DPT.
